PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The Fiat 508, nicknamed “Balilla” after an 18th Century Genoese hero, was conceived as an affordable and practical compact car. It succeeded in being precisely that, with the majority built from 1932–1937 being two-door four-seat saloons, sensible cabriolets, and light commercial vehicles. Yet the skill of the engineering team responsible for the car—led by Tranquillo Zerbi, with contributions from Antonio Fessia, Bartolomeo Nebbia, and Dante Giacosa, most of whom brought experience from Fiat’s aeronautical department—made the humble 508 an ideal platform for so much more., Fiat soon developed a more powerful version, the 508S, squeezing 30 horsepower from its 995-cubic-centimetre side-valve engine (a more powerful overhead-valve version was later offered). This model was draped in sporting bodywork from Fiat as well as a range of coachbuilders, and it contested a variety of grands prix and endurance races with success, including class wins at Le Mans and the Mille Miglia., Offered here is a 508S Coppa d’Oro, a striking two-seat spider with flowing wings and a distinctive central fin in the rear. Research conducted by a previous owner, Mike Hawke, suggested that this was one of four such cars imported to Malaysia, and that it was delivered new to a member of the Selangor Royal Family, who retained the car until 1938. Hawke’s further research suggests that this chassis may have been originally delivered with a side-valve engine and a four-speed gearbox, the latter a feature introduced in spring 1934, making for an unusual (and perhaps unique) configuration. At some point in the late 1930s, a replacement engine was fitted., The Fiat reportedly had a small number of owners—including Loke Wan Tho, the owner of Cathay Cinema and chairman of Malaysia Singapore Airlines—before it was purchased circa 1970 by Cdr Mike Hawke, who was a Naval Officer living in Malaysia at the time. By then the car needed a complete rebuild, which was carried out under the guidance of Hawke, who proceeded to use the car extensively on tours and in hill climb and grand prix events in Malaysia. When he returned to the United Kingdom with his family, he took the Fiat with him and continued to race it extensively in club events., In 1993, the 508S was acquired by David Mead via D E Baldock of Goudhurt, Kent. During Mead’s ownership the car was featured in an issue of, , which praised its sprightly nature and deemed it a “well-kept secret” with a fun-factor that far exceeds its petite size. Although originally fitted with the early production side-valve engine, Mr Mead rebuilt a later, more powerful overhead valve engine as fitted to later production models. This engine will also be sold with the car., Offered now with an appealing patina that speaks to its enthusiastic use, this characterful Fiat remains highly eligible for rallies and tours.

LOT_SUMMARY: Fascinating history; understood to have been delivered new to a member of the Selangor Royal Family of Malaysia, Acquired by an expatriate and used in grand prix and hill climb events in Malaysia in the 1970s before bringing the car to the United Kingdom, Powered by a 30 horsepower side-valve inline-four engine, which is paired with a four-speed gearbox, Attractive and athletic styling, with flowing wings and a central rear fin

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Founded in 1896 in northwestern England, the Lancashire Steam Motor Company evolved from manufacturing steam machinery into producing motorised commercial transport. The company delivered its first steam bus in 1900 and its first petrol version in 1905, before officially renaming itself Leyland Motors in 1907. Post-World War I industrial expansion catalysed the mass production of commercial buses starting in 1919. Expanding its portfolio further, the manufacturer introduced its first passenger automobile, the Leyland Eight, at the 1920 London International Motor Exhibition., This 1929 Leyland Lioness features a "Charabanc" open-top body, believed to be a later conversion after this chassis was originally built to house single-deck bus coachwork. Derived from the French phrase, , meaning carriage with benches, these open-top buses featured rows of forward-facing seats accommodating 26 to 30 passengers. The format of the Charabanc made it a popular choice for sightseeing, touring, day trips, or even weekend excursions., This bus is thought to have been delivered new to the Bradford Corporation. Later restored over the 1970s and 1980s, the engine was overhauled by S Brunt, the body by the coachbuilder S H Wyatt, the paint by C Simpson Coach Painters, all of Staffordshire, with the trim and upholstery completed by Stan Chilton of Derby. The body now fitted is understood to be of a replica construction. The restoration is believed to have been finished in 1981 and soon after the bus formed part of The James C Leake Collection in the United States and another private collection in Canada., The Lioness has since enjoyed a vibrant later life at shows and tours. It participated in the HCVS Trans Pennine tour in 2014 and the HCVS London to Brighton Run in 2017. Additionally, the bus has been featured multiple times at the Brooklands Museum, first in April 2016 at the 43rd Spring Gathering at Brooklands Museum hosted by the London Bus Museum, with return exhibitions in October 2016 and October 2018., Whether parked or on the move, this Leyland Lioness Charabanc is a charming reminder of early 20th Century travel and is sure to capture the imagination of transport enthusiasts everywhere.

LOT_SUMMARY: Delivered new to the Bradford Corporation as a single-deck bus and later converted to its current “Charabanc” body style, Restored over the 1970s and 1980s and later formed part of private collections in the United States, Canada, and United Kingdom, Participated in HCVS events including the Trans Pennine 2014 and London to Brighton Run 2017, Shown at the 43rd Spring Gathering at Brooklands Museum hosted by the London Bus Museum in April 2016, Charming example of early British mass-transportation

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Stylish, well-engineered, and affordable, the Fiat 508 was Italy’s original “people’s car”, debuting more than two decades before the popular 500 of the 1950s would assume the mantle. Produced from 1932 to 1937 with assembly spanning multiple countries, the ‘Balilla’—as it was nicknamed—became the first Fiat with production exceeding 110,000 units. It was initially offered in two-door Berlina, two-seater open Spider, and four-door open Torpedo versions, powered by a short-stroke 995-cubic-centimeter side-valve inline four-cylinder engine driving the rear wheels through a three-speed manual transmission., A lightweight, competition-oriented spider debuted in 1933 with svelte bodywork designed by Carrozzeria Ghia. It would eventually become known as the Fiat 508S ‘Balilla’ Coppa d’Oro, named after an eight-day, 3,500-mile endurance race across Italy in which the 508S proved highly successful, dominating the 1,100-cubic-centimetre class in 1934. It featured sweeping front wings, cut-down doors, a narrow cabin with passenger seat set slightly behind the driver, and a unique rear-end treatment with a single vertical fin. Early examples of the 508S ‘Balilla’ Coppa d’Oro had an uprated version of the side-valve four-cylinder engine and a three-speed gearbox. A more powerful version arrived in 1934, powered by a revised inline-four with overhead valves and a four-speed gearbox., The example offered here, fitted with the more powerful overhead-valve engine, was delivered new to Germany and is accompanied by period registration papers that verify its ownership history up to the 1960s. Believed to have later been taken to Japan, in 1998 the Fiat was acquired at auction by David Mead, a renowned car collector who had acquired another 508S five years prior. He would register the Fiat with the Vintage Sports-Car Club in 2003 and retain it as a prized possession alongside his other 508S., Though exact production figures for the 508S Coppa d’Oro remain unconfirmed, these competition-oriented variants with lightweight, hand-crafted bodywork were produced in far smaller numbers than standard 508S models. With its proven competition pedigree, it is welcomed in prestigious vintage road rallies around the globe, making this example a lovely entry into the world of vintage motoring.

LOT_SUMMARY: Restored example of the competition-oriented version of Fiat’s first “people’s car”, Attractive lightweight coachwork designed by Ghia, Delivered new to Germany and accompanied by a copy of its 1930s, Acquired at auction by its late consigning owner in 1998, Accompanied by Vintage Sports-Car Club and Fiat Register documents, Eligible for participation in vintage road rallies

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: While the Aston Martin DB5 saloon achieved worldwide fame through its association with a certain British man of mystery, the model’s more exclusive and desirable expression was reserved for a far more select clientele. Conceived for discerning owners in sunnier climates, the DB5 Convertible combined the elegance and performance of the closed DB5 with enhanced luxury, exceptional rarity, and the unique pleasures of open-air grand touring. It retained all the saloon’s mechanical strengths, most notably its 4.0-litre straight six-cylinder engine fitted with triple SU HD8 carburettors, which delivered approximately 283 horsepower and enabled a top speed exceeding 140 mph. Unlike the saloon, however, the convertible was equipped with a more comprehensive array of standard features, including a five-speed ZF transmission, power windows, reclining seats, chrome wire wheels, and expansive Connolly hides., While nearly 1,000 saloons were constructed, just 123 DB5 Convertibles were produced, elevating it from mere derivative to a true connoisseur’s choice and ensuring that today it remains one of the rarest and most coveted British cars of any type., Chassis number DB5C/1292/R, offered here, is documented by its build record as having been delivered via the Brooklands agent, finished in Goodwood Green over Fawn interior, with the 3.77:1 Power Lock rear axle. It was supplied to original owner C R Volz, Esquire, residing at the time at Kelsale Manor, a Grade II-listed building on the Main Road in Saxmundham, Suffolk, which still stands. Recorded in newspapers of the time as a gentleman farmer, Charles Robert Volz was a longstanding client of the car’s manufacturer, having previously enjoyed a Lagonda and an earlier Aston Martin., Correspondence in the file indicates that Mr Volz reported the loss of its original logbook in 1980, indicating that he had retained the motorcar for 16 years. The following year it was reported to Aston Martin as having been renovated by Blakers, a well-regarded repair firm in Finchley, with a DB6 dashboard, front sheet metal, and chassis plate fitted, apparently for a new caretaker, one R Grossmark of Hassocks. Curiously, today the DB5 now bears the engine number and chassis plate mentioned in its original build record, although the chassis frame itself is believed to be from a DB6. RM Sotheby’s will instruct a marque-specialist inspection of the car prior to the London auction and interested parties are encouraged to request a copy of the report., In any case, the DB5 Convertible subsequently passed in 1989 to Brian Charles Wigzell of Southfields, London; in 1984 to Robert D G Gibson of Glastonbury; and in 2003 to Robert Alan Heslett of Wetherby, all as recorded in official documentation included within the history file., The motorcar joined the present distinguished collection in 2011, by which time it had been properly refinished in its original, rich, and elegant livery as presented today, and has since remained garaged alongside many other superb British and European sporting automobiles of its era. With heater/defroster and Radiomobile radio, it would be a wonderful means of swift, comfortable transportation on any number of vintage tours and rallies in the years to come, just as it has been for so many of its prior caretakers.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of only 123 examples of the DB5 Convertible produced, Finished in its original livery of Goodwood Green over Fawn hides, Accompanied by a copy of its factory build records, Attractively restored and presented

sale_title: 1923 Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost Tilbury Saloon by Willoughby
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: In 1919, Rolls-Royce acquired a factory in Springfield, Massachusetts, and began to manufacture the Silver Ghost on these shores. In addition to Brewster, American Rolls-Royce were bodied by many other prestige coachbuilders, a number of them under the hallmark of Rolls-Royce Custom Coach Work. Included in this bevy of eastern craftsmanship were such companies as Biddle & Smart, Willoughby, Merrimac, and Holbrook. In order to have cars ready for customers who wished to buy “off the showroom floor”, a range of standard designs was prepared, to be built by the aforementioned firms., Chassis number 442HH, offered here, was originally fitted with an open-drive limousine body by New Haven, and supplied in August of 1923 to Samuel Frederic Houston, a prominent Pennsylvania railroad executive and industrialist, at his famous estate, Drum Moir, in the Chestnut Hill neighbourhood of Philadelphia. As regularly occurred in-period, it was eventually either traded back or reacquired by Rolls-Royce of America. In 1931 it was rebodied by Brewster with this Tilbury saloon, a Willoughby-built example originally mounted to chassis number 351LF, for a new owner, E H Glenn of Meadowbrook, Pennsylvania., The car’s next known owner, Stewart Cook of Red Bank, New Jersey, acquired it by 1953, and appears to have sold it in 1956 to H L Robbins of Wyncote, Pennsylvania. It then passed in 1959 to the well-known early American enthusiast, Alexander Stein of Byram, Connecticut, and remained with him for at least a decade. Following ownership by one James Llloyd, the car moved across the Atlantic, becoming one of the few Springfield Rolls-Royces in England under the care of James Porter of London in 1987., In 1993 the Silver Ghost was acquired in London by the present owner, and has since resided quietly in his collection in Portugal. Noted to have been unused in the last decade, it is nonetheless well-preserved cosmetically, in apparently very original condition, and boasts a wonderful and thoroughly charming patina of honesty overall. Owing to its long-term storage, bidders should note that the car will require mechanical inspection prior to being driven. It now awaits a new owner to awaken it further for touring and rally enjoyment, experiencing the quality of a well-loved Silver Ghost on British, European, or even once again North American shores.

LOT_SUMMARY: Offered from 33 years of single-family ownership, Originally delivered to prominent American industrialist Samuel Frederic Houston, Formerly owned by early enthusiasts Stewart Cook and Alexander Stein, Unseen in recent years; a wonderful ‘Springfield’ Silver Ghost in attractively patinated condition
restoration_history: rebodied by Brewster
provenance: Samuel Frederic Houston, Stewart Cook, Alexander Stein

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Lightburn made its name as a maker of cement mixers and washing machines but attempted to establish itself as a car manufacturer with the launch of the Zeta. PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The Ferrari 458 Speciale Aperta is a visceral celebration of open-air performance and engineering brilliance: an emphatic final chapter in Ferrari’s naturally aspirated, mid-engined V-8 era. Unveiled at the 2014 Paris Motor Show and limited to 499 examples worldwide, the Speciale Aperta represented the ultimate evolution of the 458 platform, uniting the razor-sharp dynamics of the 458 Speciale Berlinetta with the unfiltered drama and freedom of a retractable hardtop convertible., Beneath its muscular, aerodynamically honed bodywork lies one of Maranello’s great modern engines: a 4.5-litre naturally aspirated V-8, gloriously free-revving and capable of producing 597 brake horsepower at 9,000 rpm and 398 lb-ft of torque. A 35-brake horsepower increase over the standard 458 Italia, this extraordinary output was achieved through a remarkable 14:1 compression ratio, revised pistons, reshaped combustion chambers, and a carbon fibre intake system. Paired with Ferrari’s lightning-fast seven-speed F1 dual-clutch transmission, the Speciale Aperta accelerates from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.0 seconds and on to a top speed of around 200 mph, all accompanied by one of the defining exhaust notes of the modern Ferrari era., Ferrari left nothing to chance in ensuring that the Speciale Aperta’s dynamic ability matched its sonic drama. Formula 1- and LaFerrari-derived technology includes Side Slip Control, which continuously coordinates power delivery, the E-Diff rear differential and F1-Trac traction-control system to enhance stability and driver confidence at the limit. Recalibrated adaptive dampers, carbon-ceramic brakes, and active aerodynamic flaps work in concert to deliver exceptional cornering precision and responsiveness without sacrificing usability on the road., The rigid aluminium chassis was reinforced to preserve impressive torsional stiffness despite the absence of a fixed roof. Crafted entirely from aluminium, its retractable hardtop folds away in just 14 seconds and adds only 50 kilograms over the Speciale Berlinetta. Yet the Speciale Aperta remains more than 90 kilograms lighter than a standard 458 Spider—a testament to the obsessive weight-saving measures that defined the model. Reworked aerodynamics, including active front and rear flaps and a redesigned rear diffuser, reduced drag while preserving the downforce and high-speed composure expected of Ferrari’s most focused open V-8., This United Kingdom-delivered example is particularly notable as one half of an extraordinary factory-commissioned pairing. It was ordered alongside an identically specified 458 Speciale Berlinetta through Ferrari’s Tailor Made programme, with both cars conceived in matching liveries and closely corresponding bespoke appointments. More remarkably, the pair carry almost unheard-of sequential chassis numbers—an exceptional detail that elevates this Aperta beyond even the rarefied standard of Ferrari’s limited-production open V-8 special series. The twinned car is offered at RM Sotheby’s London auction as Lot 133., Its highly distinctive specification is centred on the rare Alluminio Grezzo Opaco finish, a satin silver treatment coated to exposed aluminium and finished with clear lacquer. A Blu Nart racing livery provides a striking competition-inspired contrast, joined by black brake callipers, titanium sports exhaust pipes, and the highly desirable Scuderia Ferrari fender shields. Exposed carbon fibre detailing appears throughout the exterior, including the rear diffuser, front air vents, engine covers, front flaps, and wheel cups. The car is also equipped with suspension lift, discreetly increasing everyday usability while preserving the uncompromising visual theatre of the Speciale Aperta., The cabin carries the same comprehensive Tailor Made theme with Alcantara used extensively across the headliner, upper and lower dashboard, wheel arches, and central tunnel to create an unmistakably purposeful environment. Medium-sized carbon fibre racing seats are upholstered in high-tech 3D fabric, finished with contrasting white stitching and white Cavallino Rampante embroidery embossed into the headrests. Additional Tailor Made and optional equipment includes a coloured steering wheel, integrated radio navigation and Bluetooth system, and parking sensors with camera., Sold new in the United Kingdom and carefully retained from new, this exceptional Speciale Aperta had covered only 1,751 miles at the time of cataloguing. It is offered with its accompanying Ferrari-issued scale model, Tailor Made ordering correspondence and Certificate of Authenticity, MoT certificates, together with service and maintenance invoices from Stratstone Ferrari of Colchester, Essex., With its exceptionally low mileage, remarkable Tailor Made specification, and exceptional connection to its sequentially numbered 458 Speciale sibling, this Aperta represents an opportunity of real distinction. Offered alongside its 458 Speciale sister car (Lot 133), the buyer of this lot will surely want to take home both Ferraris to continue their significant pairing.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of just 499 examples of the Ferrari 458 Speciale Aperta produced worldwide, Exceptionally specified through Ferrari’s Tailor Made programme in rare Alluminio Grezzo Opaco, with a Blu Nart racing livery and exposed carbon-fibre detailing, Part of an exceptional matching pair with sequential chassis numbers; twinned to a 458 Speciale, commissioned alongside it and offered at RM Sotheby’s London auction as Lot 133, Delivered new to the United Kingdom and just two owners from new; displays just 1,751 miles at the time of cataloguing, Powered by a naturally aspirated 4.5-litre V-8 producing 597 brake horsepower, The final mid-engine V-8 Ferrari styled in collaboration with Pininfarina and one of the last models to leave Maranello under the leadership of Luca di Montezemolo, Accompanied by a Ferrari-issued scale model, Tailor Made documentation, MoT certificates, and service history

sale_title: 1961 Bentley S2 Drophead Coupé Adaptation by H.J. Mulliner
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: H.J. Mulliner’s Drophead Coupé Adaptation first appeared late in the run of the Bentley S1 and Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud I, as a catalogued offering based upon factory “Standard Steel Saloon” body shells—though these were so heavily reworked that the finished product was in every sense a fully coachbuilt automobile. The elegant, subtle design of these cars made the design extremely popular on the Silver Cloud II, but many fewer examples were produced on the contemporary Bentley S2, as the majority of coachbuilt Bentleys by this time had moved to the S2 Continental chassis, which had its own unique drophead coupé design. Indeed, only 18 S2s were outfitted as Drophead Coupé Adaptations, style number 7492, 11 of them were right-hand drive., The motorcar offered here, chassis number B554CU, was ordered as stock by the London dealer Car Mart Ltd, to which it was delivered in February 1961, equipped with an automatic gearbox. Apparently either used by Car Mart for executive purposes or as a demonstrator, it was sold by them in 1963 to Sir William Steward, former Member of Parliament and longtime operator of the Veeraswamy restaurant in Regent Street. Under Sir William’s leadership, Veeraswamy expanded into prepared foods with the introduction of the first canned curry, which made the Stewards very wealthy; he was popularly known in the period press as “King Curry”., King Curry’s Bentley appears, from copies of a UK “buff” logbook on file, to have remained in its home country into the early 1970s. In 1969, it was registered to Barry Gibb, one of the brothers who made up the Bee Gees, one of the most prominent and commercially successful groups in pop music from the 1960s well into the 1980s. He was, off-stage, a longtime Bentley enthusiast, amassing a small, select gathering of vintage and modern models. The S2 was later part of the prominent Blackhawk Collection in California, before becoming part of the present owner’s excellent collection in Belgium several years ago., Restored in its handsome original livery of Shell Grey over Blue hides, as documented by copies of build sheets as well as copies of restoration photographs included in the file, the Bentley presents in lovely overall condition, clearly displaying the good care that it has received in present ownership. It is a most attractive example of its type, with rich and interesting history with fascinating personalities, as every good Bentley should have.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of only 18 Drophead Coupé Adaptations built on the S2 chassis, Originally delivered to Sir William Steward, coined “King Curry”, Formerly owned by music legend Barry Gibb of the Bee Gees, Attractively restored and presented in its original colourway

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Released in 1989, the 964 generation of Porsche’s famed 911 marked the dawn of a new era. The smoother bumpers, redesigned wheels, and retractable spoiler suggested a superficial makeover—yet 85 per cent of the car had been completely reengineered. Key updates included the 3.6-litre Type M64 flat-six, coil-spring suspension (in place of torsion bars), and improved aerodynamics., Variants included the Carrera 2, all-wheel-drive Carrera 4, and Turbo, but for 1992 Porsche developed a very special version: the Carrera RS. Inspired by its 1973 namesake, the RS was closely related to the Carrera Cup racer. Sitting 40 millimetres lower than the Carrera 2, the 260-horsepower RS featured a lightened flywheel, limited-slip differential, Cup wheels, and Turbo brakes, plus a bare-bones cockpit to keep weight down., In 1993, Porsche developed the Carrera RS even further with the ultra-exclusive RS 3.8. Built to homologate the highly successful 3.8 RSR racer, the road car is easily identified by its wide-body wheel arches, massive rear wing, and three-piece “Speedline for Porsche” wheels. Naturally, the vehicle was subjected to an extensive lightweight programme that utilised aluminium for the construction of the bonnet and doors, while the windows featured thinner glass., Following that theme, the 964's standard plush carpeting was replaced with thinner and lighter material, the rear seats were deleted, and items such as the power door locks, electric window lifts, and electric multi-adjustable seats were replaced with less weighty components. There was no sound insulation or undercoating. All told, almost 300 kilograms were saved compared to a standard, 1,500-kilogram Carrera 2., As the name implies, the model gained a 3.8-litre flat six-cylinder engine, bored out by 2 millimetres, providing 300 horsepower to the rear wheels through a strengthened six-speed manual transmission. This output results in a 0-60 mph time of just under five seconds with an ultimate top speed nudging 170 mph., The example on offer is one of just 55 produced and is believed to be the only car from the limited run finished in paint-to-sample Zermatt Silver Metallic, which was complemented by a Black leather interior. The Porsche was completed by the Stuttgart factory on 1 September 1993 and built with optional codes detailing front bucket seats, 18-inch painted RS Cup alloy wheels, widebody kit, 92-litre fuel tank, 40 per cent locking limited-slip differential, and a leather steering wheel by Atiwe., The 911 was configured for Spain (Porsche country code C27), with original delivery correspondence on file extracted from the seminal works, by Jürgen Barth, Norbert Franz, and Robert Weber. This lists the car’s exact configuration in the chassis registry section. The period correspondence notes first delivery to a Porsche VIP, and remarkably the 911 Carrera RS 3.8 has remained in their care ever since., Indeed, offered with just 10,210 kilometres showing on its odometer at the time of cataloguing, this rare and immaculately presented Porsche comes direct from its sole owner from new. Importantly, the car retains its matching-numbers type M64/04 3.8-litre engine. Bidders should note that, as the 911 has been driven so sparingly, RM Sotheby’s would encourage inspection and mechanical recommissioning prior to driving the car on the road., While the mere silhouette of this generation of 911 Carrera RS 3.8 will be familiar to marque aficionados, with its distinctive 964 shape and recognisable rear spoiler, the details of this rare Porsche add up to make it one of the most desirable of the air-cooled 911s. Not only is the RS 3.8 a thrilling sports car, but also important as an exceedingly rare modern Porsche fit for any collection.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of just 55 examples of the Carrera RS 3.8 built; the ultimate air-cooled RS, Delivered new to Spain, where it has been used sparingly by its sole owner since 1993, Believed to be the only 964-generation 911 Carrera RS 3.8 finished in paint-to-sample Zermatt Silver Metallic; Black leather interior, Originally fitted with—and still wears—18-inch RS 3.8 alloy wheels; factory bucket seats and rear spoiler enhance the sporting look, Additional original equipment includes widebody kit, 92-litre fuel tank, and leather steering wheel by Atiwe, Retains its matching-numbers 3.8-litre flat-six engine, Odometer reads just 10, 210 kilometres from new

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: In its earliest years, the Locomobile marque set up as a manufacturer of steam-engined motorcars based out of Watertown, Massachusetts. The company moved production to Bridgetown, Connecticut in 1900 and within just three years had switched its efforts entirely to internal combustion engine cars. The small steam automobiles from its foundational period proved useful to travelling professionals requiring quick mobility at the time, though, with at least 4,000 examples built from 1899 to 1902., At the height of its steam car production, Locomobile offered seven body styles of varying practicality, while the simple Runabout was billed as the affordable model for everyday use. On sale for $600 at the turn of the century, its list price equates to around $27,000 (roughly £20,000) today. A modest price but surely still a luxurious outlay for many in the advent of the automobile and at the very beginning of mass uptake to engine-propelled transport., The example offered here is a Type 1 Spindle-Seat Runabout, verified by the Veteran Car Club (VCC) as an 1899 model, and believed to originate from the first 200 cars made by Locomobile. The steam car is steered by central tiller, final drive is by a single blockchain, and the brakes operate on an open-type differential. It is believed that the steam car was first delivered to New York and is said to have been returned to the factory in 1902 for the fitment of an Ottoway burner rated at around 7 horsepower and later water gauge glass. It was driven until it was damaged around 1910. The car was laid up and removed from storage, largely intact, in the late 1930s. Then, in the mid-1970s, it was discovered again by a steam car enthusiast. It is thought that the car was taken to England around this time to participate in the London to Brighton Veteran Car Run and VCC events. With its owner, the Locomobile appeared in a 1977 feature in, , yet by the early 1980s it failed a boiler inspection and was mothballed., The Locomobile was acquired at auction in 2000 and, after decades of being stored in a dismantled state, its new owner made efforts to recommission the steam car with the installation of a new ‘Gould’ boiler in 2001; they retained possession until 2014, when it was acquired by the consigning owner. With the vendor, the Locomobile has been enjoyed as a distinguishable entrant on the London to Brighton Veteran Car Run (pictured on file participating in 2016), as well as other events. Sure to command an early start time on the dash to the south coast owing to its pre-1900 build date, as well as being eligible for many other VCC events, this characterful steam car awaits its next owner for enjoyment in future outings.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Celebrating Ferrari’s relentless pursuit of performance, the Scuderia Spider 16M takes its name from Maranello’s 16th Formula 1 Constructors’ World Championship title—an achievement unrivalled in motorsport. Ferrari forged its reputation through on-track triumphs, so it is only fitting that one of the company’s finest modern creations honours its success at the highest level of racing., Built in a limited series of just 499 examples, the Scuderia Spider 16M derives from Ferrari’s uncompromising 430 Scuderia. The exclusively open-top 16M retains the latter’s potent 4.3-litre V-8 but adds subtle refinements, including redesigned pistons and a higher compression ratio. The result is an engine that climbs to redline with thrilling immediacy, delivering torque and roar in equal measure. Rated by Ferrari at 503 horsepower and paired with its acclaimed F1-SuperFast2 six-speed transmission, the engine delivers scorching acceleration, sprinting from 0 to 60 mph in just 3.8 seconds and topping out at 196 mph., Despite the structural reinforcements required for its open-top design, the 16M remains astonishingly light, a testament to Ferrari’s focus on weight reduction. Engineers implemented a comprehensive diet, which included lightened front and rear bumpers, reworked front suspension and steering, forged alloy wheels unique to the model, a carbon fibre roll bar, and titanium wheel bolts. Through these measures, the 16M sheds a remarkable 80 kilograms compared to the standard F430 Spider, preserving the dynamic experience of the 430 Scuderia while delivering the thrill of open-air driving., Delivered new to Japan, this Ferrari Scuderia Spider 16M was sold in August 2009 to its first owner, a resident of Musashino City on the western side of the Tokyo metropolis. Completed with a superbly curated list of options from the factory, the car is finished in the classic colour Grigio Scuro with hand-painted Italian Tricolore stripe streaking down the centre. The presentation is enhanced by yellow brake callipers contrasting nicely under the gunmetal alloy wheels, which are additionally complemented by the Scuderia shields affixed to the wings. With the inclusion of the carbon fibre exterior package, the Ferrari’s appearance expresses the high-performance nature of the Scuderia Spider 16M., The cockpit is trimmed in Blu Scuro Alcantara with white contrast stitching and yellow mesh seat inserts, which creates a distinct, yet complementary tonal space compared to the exterior. Key highlights include lightweight carbon fibre racing seats and an Alcantara steering wheel with carbon fibre shift paddles that bring the Scuderia’s F1–derived technology directly to the driver’s fingertips, further to a rare white rev counter. More visceral still than the much-lauded tin-top 430 Scuderia, the 16M is both a modern masterpiece and a machine that any true, must experience at least once.

description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis number 23UB is recorded in its factory build records as being a sought-after late-production “parallel bonnet” example finished to London-to-Edinburgh specification, complete with high compression pistons, and was originally mounted with a limousine by Barker. It was intended for delivery to Sir George Riddel, but this was prevented by World War I and the car was instead on active service with the British military until at least 1919, with regular services noted in factory records., In 1960 the car was rediscovered by avid Silver Ghost enthusiast Lars de Jounge, having been used as a commercial vehicle on a British farm. It was subsequently acquired in 1998 by Fred Buess, member of a family long active in Rolls-Royce enthusiasm and restoration in Southern California since the 1940s., A noted second-generation specialist in the Silver Ghost model, Mr Buess undertook a full restoration of the car, during which it was crowned with a magnificent Labourdette-inspired skiff body, constructed beautifully using correct materials and build processes to duplicate a body originally mounted to chassis number 2EB, pictured in John Fasal’s well-known work, . Skiff bodies were the ultimate of their era, built using wood, which may be called the carbon fibre of the Jazz Age; it was the lightest but strongest material available. The body was built using transverse internal ribs of wood, covered in strips of steam-bent wood secured by many hundreds of individual brass rivets, then sanded and varnished in the manner of a classic wooden boat. It resulted in featherweight coachwork for maximum performance., Indeed, beauty was not only skin-deep; information on file indicates that the car was fully mechanically sorted, as well, including being prepared for high-speed touring with optimised compression, porting, and valves, billet connecting rods, and 3.06:1 differential gearing., At its completion in 2001, the Silver Ghost was exhibited at the famed Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, receiving the coveted trophy for Most Elegant Open Car. Its magnificence was further recogniaed with Best of Show honours at several other West Coast concours d’elegance, and it was featured in numerous publications, including, and, , as well as alongside some of the world’s most spectacular automobiles in the Petersen Automotive Museum’s 2002 exhibition, Million Dollar Cars., In 2008 the car was purchased by a well-known Dutch enthusiast, from whose collection it is now offered. During his ownership it had its engine rebuilt by Glew Ltd and fitted with a 12-volt starter for ease of operation, as noted in descriptions of work and invoices on file. Afterwards, it has been much enjoyed with numerous exhibitions throughout Europe and England, winning First Prize at the RREC Annual Rally at Rockingham Castle in 2014. Furthermore it has been used as intended, running some 20,000 miles in international tours and rallies, including 20 Ghost Club rallies in Slovenia, Croatia, Italy, Denmark, Sweden, Latvia, Estonia, Finland, the Iberian Peninsula, and the Netherlands. The Rolls-Royce is now offered from a deceased estate., Simply put, few surviving “parallel bonnet” Silver Ghosts are of the London-to-Edinburgh specification, and fewer still have been fitted with what might well be considered the ultimate coachwork, built in the lightest materials for maximum performance. It is, in every sense, a supercar of its period, and a road and touring machine par excellence.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The Milwaukee Automobile Company was of numerous firms organised in the Midwestern United States, that cradle of early automaking, during the early 1900s. It came and went virtually in the same breath—established in 1900, it was bankrupt by 1902. Nonetheless, in its brief life, it built some fascinating steam-powered motorcars, none more interesting than this 1901 model., Reportedly designed by Chicago agent Frank P Illsley for local resident Dr J G Lovell, it was featured at that year’s Chicago Auto Show, and described in the period press as having been built to achieve “a speed of a mile a minute…It is expected to be the fastest automobile in America, and of its kind, the fastest in the world.” Numerous distinctive features described in the period press on the Racer, including chassis and running gear modifications with additional front-end bracing and a yolk brace between rear axle and engine, remain on the motorcar. One wonders if Dr Lovell actually intended to race, or just wanted what amounted to a Veteran supercar; it may have participated in one event in Joliet, Illinois in October 1901, but appears to have not otherwise competed in anger., Subsequently, the Milwaukee was modified to be of more modern design, with a later body and the boiler relocated under a more traditional front end. In this form, the car reappeared in 1954 in the care of early enthusiast Ray Salentine of Waukesha, Wisconsin, who undertook its original restoration. The car later moved to an owner in Beloit, Illinois, then disappeared, eventually reappearing in a museum in Ladenburg, Germany in the early 21st Century., In 2005 the steamer was acquired by a new owner, who undertook considerable research to restore the car back to its 1901 design. The Milwaukee was dated by the Veteran Car Club in 2011 and is accompanied by its detailed report and certificate, while the Steam Racer has been a multiple entrant to the London to Brighton Veteran Car Run in 2010, 2011, and 2024. In 2019, a new boiler was manufactured and fitted by the noted specialist J R Goold Steam Ltd. Importantly, in 2025 it underwent a successful boiler examination and pressure test, which remains valid through to December of this year., This is a most fascinating Veteran steamer, with great heritage and power in equal amounts.

Introduced in 1988, the E34 M5 combined the practicality of the 5 Series with the engineering expertise of BMW M GmbH and, importantly, represented the final generation of M5 to be hand-built in this manner., Each E34 M5 began life as a bodyshell at BMW’s Dingolfing plant before being transferred to BMW M GmbH in Garching, where it was completed by hand. description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud III represented a watershed moment for its manufacturer. It was still a traditionally crafted luxury automobile with wood-framed bodywork featuring a library’s worth of burled walnut; the engine was reassuringly silent; and the interior was surpassingly comfortable. The engine, improved over the previous Silver Cloud II, was the epitome of the Rolls-Royce ideal of gradual refinement of a design. Yet this model also represented the company’s first nods towards contemporary styling, with quad headlamps, a lowered hood and radiator shell, smaller bumpers, and separate front seats., No offering better exemplified the Silver Cloud III’s straddling of two worlds than the Drophead Coupé Adaptation, crafted by Rolls-Royce’s coachbuilding shop, H.J. Mulliner. A continuation of the similar style introduced extremely late in Silver Cloud I production and used exclusively on the Silver Cloud II, it was known as an “Adaptation” because it was based on factory Standard Steel Saloon body panels and inner structure. So thoroughly massaged and reworked were the factory components, however, that the end result was truly a piece of coachbuilt craftsmanship as fine as any fully custom body., Not long into the Silver Cloud III’s production run, modernity took firm hold at Rolls-Royce with the debut of a Drophead Coupé of brand-new, audacious design. Thus, the Silver Cloud III Drophead Coupé Adaptation enjoyed a very limited run and was scarce even when new, with just 37 examples produced—only 12 were right-hand drive., The car offered here, chassis number SEV11, was delivered in August 1963 by prominent London dealer HR Owen to Charles Spreckley & Company Ltd, a London contracting and shopfitting firm, presumably for the use of its principal. It subsequently moved across the Atlantic with its 1985 acquisition by Donald T Knutson of Minneapolis, Minnesota. A later restoration was undertaken by the noted P&A Wood, to its typical excellent level of quality and detail, with the colourway of Caribbean Blue over Parchment hides with matching hood; an invoice on file notes that at the time nearly £195,000 was spent. Subsequently the car was acquired, through the auspices of P&A Wood, by the well-known Belgian collector Bob Lalement, and has since remained in Belgium, most recently as part of a select but well-chosen collection of coachbuilt Bentleys from which it is now offered., Simply, this is a beautiful example of perhaps the most sought-after coachwork on the Silver Cloud III, benefitting from excellent long-term care within fine collections.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: As 1993 rolled into view, Lamborghini sought to celebrate its 30th birthday by introducing a special-edition model based on the mid-engined Diablo poster star. Christened the SE30, it retained the legendary V-12 displacing 5.7 litres but gained a revised fuel system, magnesium intake manifolds, and a free-flow exhaust for an increased output of 525 horsepower., Unlike the contemporary Diablo VT, the SE30 zeroed in on its raw character courtesy of a rear-wheel-drive-only platform and mighty 180-kilogram weight saving. Bordering on being a road-legal competition car, it sported carbon fibre body panels (a product of Horacio Pagani’s composite materials department), race-specification brakes and seats, plexiglass windows, and ditched the air conditioning and power steering as part of the crash diet. The results spoke for themselves. Aided by a tall first gear, the Diablo SE30 could launch from 0 to 60 mph in four seconds before hitting the magical 200 mph mark., For those fortunate enough to spot, let alone own an SE30, it was identifiable by its more aggressive and aerodynamic stance. The front bumper was redesigned to feature new intakes to the cool the brakes, the rear wing sprouted a cutting-edge active flap for improved downforce, while a raised and slatted engine cover appeared to extend the roof line., Production of the anniversary-celebrating Diablo SE30 supercar stretched to just 150 units, with 25 of those destined for the North American market. Furthermore, according to the Lamborghini build ledger, just 25 units were originally configured in right-hand-drive form. From that small allocation, a mere nine cars were to be supplied to the United Kingdom., The example on offer was ordered new by the royal family of Brunei. Completed by the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory on 26 June 1995, it was specified with striking Bianco Impacto paintwork over a Bleu Alcantara interior. Just three other Diablo SE30s were finished in this colour combination, but this car stands alone as the sole right-hand-drive example., The Diablo SE30 was delivered to the UK via Lamborghini GB on 28 July and collected on 1 August, with the car soon departing for Brunei, where it remained until the early 2000s. Purchased by Sir Colin Giltrap—the automotive magnate who supported the careers of rising motorsport stars Earl Bamber, Scott Dixon, Shane van Gisbergen, and Brendon Hartley—the Diablo SE30 moved to New Zealand, where it was registered from September 2002. The Giltrap Group owned and operated the Lamborghini Auckland dealership, always maintaining the vehicle to the highest standards. The Diablo was acquired via Lamborghini Auckland by the consigning owner in March 2006. The bill of sale on file records that the SE30 had driven circa just 2,890 kilometres at the time of purchase., In its stunning colour combination of Bianco Impacto over Bleu Alcantara, the Diablo SE30 was enjoyed on the open roads in the early years of ownership. It was later placed into storage, being driven on average 120 kilometres a year and treated to regular servicing at Lamborghini Auckland. Cherished and dutifully maintained while under the care of the vendor, the SE30 was fitted with the current Momo steering wheel so that the original item—which is supplied with the car and, for the SE30, features the same badge as seen on the 350 GT—would not wear out. Similarly, soon after buying chassis number RLA12122, the owner sourced a new-old stock SE30 car cover, plus blue race-style harnesses and matching blue seat belt straps, through Lamborghini Auckland., As part of its continued maintenance history with the official Lamborghini dealership, the Diablo SE30 had its rear brakes serviced in June 2017 and a new front-left wheel bearing was fitted in April 2024. Most recently, an engine oil and filter service was performed in March 2026, at which time the brake fluid was also renewed. A repair order history report and invoices for these works are available to view on file., In addition to the original steering wheel and car cover, this Diablo SE30 is accompanied by a complete set of owner’s guides including the warranty manual in the leather folio. Sparingly driven throughout the last two decades, it displays a modest 12,396 kilometres (approximately 7,700 miles) on the odometer at the time of cataloguing., From the limited production run of Diablo SE30s, this car possesses a unique history. A car not flouted publicly but cherished quietly during its life, the Diablo now emerges as one of the most fascinating right-hand-drive SE30s built, and one that has never before been offered for public sale., For its standing as a Lamborghini flagship V-12 supercar, any example of the rare Diablo SE30 is certain to attract admiration. But the compelling backstory of chassis RLA12122, alongside its colour specification and low use, ensures that it will be at the very centre of attention wherever it is driven or displayed.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of just nine UK-supplied right-hand-drive examples from the limited run of 150 Diablo SE30s, Ordered new by the royal family of Brunei and later purchased by New Zealand collector Sir Colin Giltrap, Presents in its spectacular factory colour combination of Bianco Impacto over Bleu Alcantara, Offered out of discreet long-term ownership in New Zealand; acquired by the vendor in 2006, Supplied with owner’s guides and warranty card in leather folio, car cover, seat belt covers, racing harnesses, and original steering wheel, The odometer displays 12,396 kilometres (approximately 7,700 miles) at the time of cataloguing

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The original “Nebula” internal codename for what would eventually become the Valkyrie was entirely fitting. Aerospace-grade engineering runs awash throughout this fully carbon fibre, road-legal hypercar that is capable of single-seater racer levels of performance. The letters in “Nebula” also denoted the key stakeholders involved: multiple Formula 1 World Championship-winning car designer Adrian Newey, Red Bull Racing, and Aston Martin., A seven-year gestation period for the Valkyrie (the name derived from Norse mythology) reflected the project’s immense complexity. Elegant bodywork, featuring the trademark Aston Martin grille shape, does without unsightly aerodynamic devices. An emphasis was placed instead on the open underfloor that employs Venturi tunnels running either side of the teardrop-shaped cockpit to feed an enormous diffuser. For this attempt at creating a Grand Prix car for the streets, extreme management of the airflow allows the Valkyrie to achieve over 3.5-G through high-speed corners, approximately three times that of a conventional sports car. All told, it can generate a genuinely tyre-bursting two tonnes of downforce., Under the skin, there’s no steel to be found in the structure of the car. To achieve the best power-to-weight ratio, carbon fibre dominates the chassis, of which the engine is a fully stressed member. Rather than conventional mounts that dampen the experience, the 65-degree, naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V-12 is attached directly to the monocoque with four bolts. Created by Cosworth, who started on the project by developing a straight-three unit, the engine has a screaming red line of some 11,100 rpm. Fitted with an electric motor and a battery pack supplied by Rimac, the Valkyrie develops a total of 1,160 horsepower. This is sent to the rear wheels only via a Ricardo-manufactured seven-speed sequential gearbox., Underlining the engineering boundaries being pushed throughout, Aston Martin says the rear brake light is the smallest and brightest ever fitted to a production car. What’s more, there are a reported 15,187 adjustable parameters across the Valkyrie. This led to the fitment of a hydraulics system with 17 different actuators borrowed from a Boeing Apache helicopter to keep pace with the active aerodynamics, double-wishbone suspension, and damping., Then there’s the single windscreen wiper. While it was initially thought that the model might do without, the potential for a Valkyrie to one day be caught at a set of red lights in a downpour led Aston Martin to find a company that could provide a sleek unit that would not spoil the silhouette but would still clean the curved windscreen. As a result, after a year of investigation into the wiper alone, the car uses the same supplier as the Space Shuttle programme., From the limited-production run of 150 road-going Valkyrie Coupés, the example offered here was built for the Asia-Pacific region in left-hand-drive form ahead of delivery to the consigning owner in Japan. The vendor’s extensive and beautiful configuration added almost £235,000 to the original list price of £2.5 million plus taxes. sale_title: 1964 Ferrari 250 GT/L Berlinetta Lusso by Scaglietti
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Introduced at the 1962 Paris Salon, Ferrari’s 250 GT/L was undoubtedly one of the most attractive grand touring cars ever built. Intended as a replacement for the 250 GT coupé, the “L” stood for Lusso, the Italian word for “luxury”, and featured an all-new interior arrangement highlighted by a revised dash panel and leather upholstery throughout the cabin. Built to cross continents in unrivalled style while cossetting a driver, passenger, and plenty of luggage, it looked simply stunning while sitting still and just as beautiful at speed., Mechanically, Ferrari’s Tipo 168 U engine was the ultimate development of the short-block Colombo 3.0-litre V-12, featuring outside-plug ignition and single-cylinder porting that had proven so successful in the 250 Testa Rossa and California Spider. Further improvements were made to the chassis including four-wheel disc brakes, coil-over shock absorbers at all four corners, and a rear Watts linkage that had been perfected on the 250 GTO., While the bodywork itself was designed by Pininfarina, the construction of it was carried out by Scaglietti and it is truly among the pair’s very best work. Boasting Ferrari’s now-typical egg-crate grille, its delicately curved fenders gave way to a bright, airy cabin and flowed into a fastback “Kamm tail". Originally owned by jet-set luminaries and celebrities, such as Steve McQueen, the Lusso was built in a modest quantity of just 350 examples over roughly two years of production. The GT/L has since evolved into one of Maranello’s most collectable production models, essentially the final and most developed evolution of the revered 250 GT lineage., The example offered here is noted to be the 316th built from the model’s 350-strong production run. Destined for the United Kingdom, the Ferrari was accordingly constructed in right-hand drive, and was the 19th of only 23 examples of the 250 Lusso made with the steering wheel on the right side. In anticipation of its British delivery, the car was fitted by the factory with a speedometer reading in miles., The Ferrari factory received the order for the Lusso from the Egham-based import business Maranello Concessionaires Ltd, with the great Ferrari privateer and head of the importer Colonel Ronnie Hoare giving a personal demonstration in another 250 GT/L to Mr Martin Brain, the first owner of chassis number 5711 GT. Mr Brain, of Sutton Coldfield, Warwickshire, had met with Colonel Hoare towards the end of 1963 and by 7 November of that year, the pair sealed the deal for a Berlinetta Lusso which was initially specified to be made with Oro Chiaro paint, Dark Red Connolly leather, Dark Red carpets, Fawn roof lining, and a Motorola radio. It was scheduled for a February 1964 build slot with delivery anticipated in late-February or early March. Mr Brain intended to part exchange a Facel Vega HK500 as part of the deal., However, some two-and-a-half weeks after placing the order, Mr Brain wrote to Maranello Concessionaires having changed his mind. Instead, he wished to change the order for the ‘colour scheme to read as Ferrari red, cream upholstery, and dark red carpets’. It is thought that the factory returned the car with a White interior, and as such is the only 250 GT/L to leave Maranello with White hide. The Ferrari was duly registered on the United Kingdom registration “ALP 5B” on 13 April 1964. Regrettably, its first owner did not retain the car for long and by 5 November of that year the Ferrari had been sold to Mr John Moore of Hereford, who put forward a rare Zagato-bodied Bristol 406 in exchange, with the deal transacted by Maranello Concessionaires. Mr Moore embarked upon an ambitious drive to Morocco with the Ferrari, returning in 1966., By July 1969, the car was sold again to one F W J Cornwallis of Eastbourne, East Sussex, and is thought to have later entered the collection of pre-eminent Ferrari enthusiast Dick Crossthwaite. The car’s earliest history is documented by period order forms and correspondence kindly provided by The Maranello Concessionaires Archive, available to view in full on file. By the late 1980s, the Ferrari is said to have been restored by Kevin O’Rourke’s Moto Technique workshop and around the same time it appeared in the April 1988 edition of, magazine. In the early 1990s, the car entered the collection of Lee Kun-hee, former Chairman of Samsung, and by the late 2000s the car was known to be in long-term ownership in Australia., In 2026, the Lusso was certified by Ferrari Classiche, which confirms the car retains its matching-numbers V-12 “Colombo” engine, gearbox, and rear differential. Today, the Ferrari presents in a condition that would invite restoration to be overseen by its next owner, offering an exciting opportunity to renew this storied factory one-off 250 GT/L.

LOT_SUMMARY: The 316th of a total 350 examples built of the 250 Lusso and the 19th of 23 right-hand-drive cars, Ordered new as a one-off factory colour combination in Rosso Cina over Pelle Bianco; the only 250 GT Lusso ordered with Pelle Bianco interior, Imported new to the UK by Maranello Concessionaires, Accompanied by copies of its original order forms plus period correspondence between Maranello Concessionaires with first few owners, Restored by Kevin O’Rourke’s MotoTechnique in the UK over 1987-88 and featured in an April 1988, magazine article, Certified by Ferrari Classiche in 2026; shown to retain its original chassis, engine, gearbox, and rear differential

sale_title: 1953 Jaguar C-Type Recreation by Brazell Engineering
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Through to the new millennium, only Porsche and Ferrari counted more outright wins in the 24 Hours of Le Mans than Jaguar. Flying the endurance racing flag for the United Kingdom, the marque’s run to seven victories was ignited by the iconic C-Type. The shapely sportscar claimed the spoils of glory at its first attempt in 1951; doubling that tally in 1953 earned the team a telegram from Queen Elizabeth II. Just 53 examples were originally constructed, with five-time Formula 1 World Champion Juan Manuel Fangio among the customers., A beautifully realised homage to a competition great, this C-Type Recreation was commissioned by the vendor and built by Brazell Engineering in Daventry across 2012 and 2013. It was formed around a chassis (number 006) sourced from Jaguar specialist Lynx and dressed in hand-formed coachwork by Shapecraft. Under the skin sits a John Exley 3.4-litre straight-six engine with correct-type cylinder block and head, rated to deliver over 280 brake horsepower. The running gear is made complete by sand-cast H8 SU carburettors, a C-Type sump, Kent 460 cams, Moss closed-ratio gear set and C-Type top cover, Pearson Engineering rear axle fitted with 3.54 crown wheel and pinion, Thornton power lock differential, Orson half-shafts and hubs, and period-design aluminium race fuel tank. Stopping power is provided by race-specification drum brakes., Registered in the United Kingdom, wearing a number plate appropriately issued in period in Coventry, this C-Type Recreation is accompanied by an FIA Historic Technical Passport valid until 31 December 2026. It featured in the Vintage Sports-Car Club-organised Pomeroy Trophy at Silverstone in February 2019, for which it was driven by David Brazell himself., Invoices in the history file show routine maintenance and inspections were entrusted to Brazell Engineering and M&C Wilkinson in South Yorkshire. It is presented in Works livery British Racing Green and sporting Old English White roundels over period-correct suede green leather showing delightful patina and custom-made tonneau cover. This FIA-correct tribute to one of the great 1950s sportscars is poised to excite its next owner both on the public roads and out on track.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: At the Paris Salon in October 1964 Ferrari introduced the 275 model line, consisting of a closed, (GTB) and an open spider (GTS)—both of which were designed by Pininfarina. Production of the, form was licensed to Scaglietti, while responsibility for the open-topped cars remained with Pininfarina’s factory in Grugliasco., The Spider was completely different in appearance and proportion to its closed sibling, and it was constructed of steel with aluminium doors, hood, and trunk lid. Uncovered headlamps, triple-louvered wings, a tapered rear end, and standard Borrani wire wheels were the Spider’s major physical identifiers beyond the cloth top, and those features were eventually carried over to the 330 and 365 GTS variants which followed. Underneath this unique skin, though, the 275 GTS bears identical mechanical components as the performance-oriented 275 GTB, including a rear transaxle that minimised weight and optimised distribution of mass. As a result, both body styles of this exceptional model share a legendary reputation for superb balance., Only 200 examples of the 275 GTS were built over an 18-month period of production, making the model far rarer than its closed sibling. Prized by marque enthusiasts today as the luxurious grand touring expression of the celebrated 3.3-litre “Columbo” 60-degree V-12 platform producing 260 brake horsepower at 7,000 rpm, the 275 GTS has evolved into one of the era’s most collectable open Ferraris., The example offered here was the 61st made from the build run that comprised only 200 cars. It was the seventh of only 19 right-hand-drive 275 GTS. With its steering its speedometer reading in miles, the Ferrari was destined for delivery to the United Kingdom. Here, it was imported by Colonel Ronnie Hoare’s legendary Maranello Concessionaires concern, being presented by the Maranello factory in Rosso Cina paintwork over a Beige leather upholstery. Today, the 275 GTS retains this iconic factory-correct colour pairing., Chassis number 07293 was delivered to its first owner, one Charles Lucas, in August 1965. Shortly afterwards it was registered for the road with the United Kingdom number plates “GGO 491C”. By 1967, the 275 GTS had been sold to R G Bond of Cheshire and, in 1972, it was acquired by R Hands of London. Bernard Kain bought the Ferrari in 1974 and kept hold of it for the next 11 years. From 1985 to 1990, the Spider was owned by noted collector Adrian Liddell of Hampshire before later coming into the ownership of Joseph Fung, a resident of Hong Kong with a car collection domiciled in England., In the care of Mr Fung, over 1994 and 1995 the Ferrari was entrusted to European Auto Restoration (now trading as European Collectibles), based in Costa Mesa, California for full and no-expense-spared restoration. The process is detailed in impressive detail by four weighty photo album folders with accompanying dated correspondence, which are offered alongside the rest of the car’s impressive history files. Mr Fung took the car to Hong Kong, where it was registered as “FR 275”. Mr Fung later returned the Ferrari to the United Kingdom for permanent storage. The car was subsequently presented for renewed restoration work undertaken by Brick Kiln Group of Wantage, who conducted concours-quality renovation for the Ferrari. Around the mid-2000s, the engine was rebuilt by Chris Holley and the Light Car Company., Chassis number 07293 was certified by Ferrari Classiche in April 2010 and is accompanied at auction with its important “Red Book”. In 2012 the 275 GTS was acquired by its consigning owner, who has continued to maintain and uphold this important Ferrari, with around 1,000 miles accrued in their care. Offered with a meticulously documented history file, matching-numbers chassis, engine, and gearbox, factory-correct colour combination, and Ferrari Classiche certification, this highly sought-after open-topped Prancing Horse awaits its next owner for prime convertible V-12 enjoyment.

LOT_SUMMARY: A rare opportunity to acquire a stunning and very rare V-12 Spider from the golden era of Ferrari, The 61st of 200 examples built of the 275 GTS; the seventh made from 19 right-hand-drive cars, Delivered new to the United Kingdom via Maranello Concessionaires in July 1965, Offered in its factory-correct colour combination of Rosso Cina over a Pelle Beige Connolly leather interior, Subject to a full restoration by California-based European Auto Restoration over 1994 and 1995; exhaustively detailed by four accompanying photo folders with dated correspondence, Later restored again to concours-standard quality by Brick Kiln Group of Wantage, Engine rebuilt by Chris Holley and Light Car Company in the early 2000s, Retained by the vendor since 2012; known ownership history from new, Certified by Ferrari Classiche in April 2010 and accompanied by its important “Red Book”; recognised to retain its matching-numbers chassis, engine, and gearbox, Supported by a history report by marque expert Marcel Massini, Ferrari 275 books and manuals in a leather folio, plus leather tool roll

description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis number B162UM started life in 1953 as a Bentley R-Type Saloon, a platform largely based on the outgoing Mark VI. Just 2,323 examples were built between 1952 and 1955. The car, per factory data card copies, was delivered new in Paris to Baronne de la Rochette wearing two-tone Masons Black and Tudor Grey paintwork over Fawn hide. Recorded to be in French ownership from at least 1995, the car was purchased by the consigning owner in October 2023. Holding a clear appreciation for world-class engineering and British classics, they submitted it to Racing Green Engineering in South Wales for a total reinvention., Specialising in “automotive nostalgia”, Racing Green was tasked with transforming chassis B162UM into a stunning recreation of what has become known as the Bentley ‘Blue Train’. Famously, then Bentley chairman Woolf Barnato drove through the night from Cannes to London in a four-door Speed Six Weymann saloon to beat the Le Train Bleu. However, thanks to being immortalised in Terence Cuneo’s painting, the car more often associated with this legendary feat is the svelte three-seater coupé styled by Gurney Nutting. While that machine would indeed become another personal car of Barnato’s, he didn’t take delivery of the grand tourer until weeks after the dates of the Le Train Bleu race., But with the Gurney Nutting coupé now firmly entrenched in automotive folklore, chassis B162UM was painstakingly rebodied in aluminium to resemble its striking proportions. As part of the overhaul, the original straight-six engine was replaced by a B81 straight-eight, the higher-performance offering from Racing Green. Displacing 6,516 cc, it is mated to a Bentley Turbo-sourced three-speed automatic transmission. The vendor, who commissioned the project, further requested the installation of heated seats, Nickel-rimmed headlights, under-bonnet LED lighting, a boot-mounted tool kit, and no fewer than three integrated drinks cabinets (one for sparkling wine, one for flat wine, and another for spirits)., The entire recreation process documented in an accompanying build folder, chassis B162UM was completed in August 2025 with Green coachwork over a Light Tan leather interior featuring burr walnut trim. The vendor is quick to praise how easily the Bentley is to operate, thanks to its torquey engine, automatic transmission, and disc brakes that make light work of long-distance drives and modern traffic., Fittingly offered for sale at RM Sotheby’s London Auction—held in partnership with the Royal Automobile Club, whose Pall Mall headquarters was Barnato’s destination on 13 March 1930—this show-stopping Bentley B Special ‘Blue Train' Recreation would make for a magnificent addition to any collection of vintage automobiles.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Introduced at the 2013 Frankfurt Motor Show, the Ferrari 458 Speciale is indeed special. Though quite similar in appearance to the 458 Italia, the mid-engine supercar benefits from numerous advancements that elevate its performance to another level. Developed with an uncompromising focus, the Speciale combined advanced aerodynamics, sophisticated electronic systems, and extensive weight-saving measures with the extraordinary character of Ferrari’s 4.5-litre V-8., Ferrari’s engineers extensively reworked the F136 engine, incorporating competition-derived components and a remarkable 14:1 compression ratio. The result was 597 brake horsepower, a 9,000 rpm redline and, at launch, the most powerful naturally aspirated V-8 ever produced by Ferrari. Its sensationally immediate throttle response and soaring soundtrack were matched by a breadth of chassis technology: an F1 dual-clutch transmission, adaptive magnetorheological dampers, E-Diff rear differential, and the pioneering Side Slip Control system. Active aerodynamic flaps at the front and rear continually balanced downforce and drag, helping the Speciale achieve exceptional stability and real-world usability., This exceptional UK-delivered example is made all the more significant by its remarkable relationship with an identically specified 458 Speciale Aperta. Commissioned together as an extraordinary matching pair through Ferrari’s Tailor Made programme, the two cars share their distinctive livery and extensive bespoke appointments; more remarkably still, they carry virtually unprecedented sequential chassis numbers. The Speciale therefore offers not merely an unusually specified example of Ferrari’s celebrated track-focused V-8, but one half of a uniquely conceived factory-commissioned duo. The 458 Speciale Aperta is also offered at RM Sotheby’s London sale as Lot 132., Its exterior is finished in the rare and arresting Alluminio Grezzo Opaco, a satin silver treatment to exposed aluminium that is sealed by clear lacquer. A Blu Nart racing stripe provides a vivid visual connection to Ferrari competition tradition, while black brake callipers, Scuderia wing shields and titanium sports exhaust pipes complete the purposeful presentation. Extensive exposed carbon-fibre detailing encompasses the rear diffuser, front air vents, engine covers, front flaps, and wheel-cup details while a suspension-lift system further enhances practicality., The Tailor Made treatment continues throughout the cockpit, which is extensively appointed in Alcantara across the headliner, upper dashboard, wheel arches, and central tunnel. Medium-sized carbon-fibre racing seats are upholstered in high-tech Mycro Prestige fabric and finished with contrasting white stitching, while white Cavallino Rampante embroidery is embossed into the headrests. Further carefully selected equipment includes a coloured steering wheel, roll bar, integrated radio-navigation and Bluetooth system, and parking camera. Together, these details create a cabin of unusually deliberate character—every element selected to complement the exterior’s competition-inspired theme., Retained by only two owners from new, this Speciale had covered just 1,980 miles at the time of cataloguing. It is accompanied by a Ferrari-issued scale model, Tailor Made order documentation, MoT certificates, and a file of service and maintenance invoices from Stratstone Ferrari of Colchester, Essex offering insight into to the car’s careful stewardship., More than simply a low-mileage 458 Speciale, this is a uniquely commissioned Ferrari—one half of an extraordinary sequentially numbered pair, conceived together and finished to an exceptionally personal brief. The buyer of this lot will surely wish to take the pair, with the 458 Speciale Aperta also up for auction as Lot 132. With its evocative exposed-aluminium aesthetic, competition-inspired detailing and unmistakable naturally aspirated V-8 soundtrack, it is a captivating expression of one of Ferrari’s great modern supercars, preserved in remarkable condition and ready to be appreciated for generations to come.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Five years into the lifecycle of Lamborghini’s flagship Aventador, the Sant’Agata marque revealed the S model to improve on the standard car with both aesthetic and performance upgrades. Lamborghini engineers fine-tuned the V-12 motor, increasing output from 691 to 730 brake horsepower, making for a top speed of 217 mph. The Aventador S gained four-wheel steering, permanent four-wheel drive, and updated suspension. Not long after the upgraded S had proven its worth in coupé form, Lamborghini followed suit with the Aventador S Roadster—announced at the 2017 Frankfurt International Motor Show., The Aventador S Roadster was mechanically identical to its hard-top sibling but gained 50 kilograms from chassis reinforcements made to facilitate the open roof, meaning that 0.3 seconds were lost to the coupé in a 0-62 mph sprint. Both cars shared the same top speed. Designed with cutting-edge technologies to prevent any further increase, the Roadster featured two detachable carbon fibre roof panels weighing just six kilograms (and shaped to be stowable in the front luggage compartment). With the roof removed, the sheer excitement of Lamborghini’s V-12 sounding along the open road would surely outweigh the split seconds counted in factory performance statistics., This example left the Sant’Agata assembly line finished in Nero Pegaso paint over an interior configured in Nero Ade with Sabbia Nefertem leather upholstery. An options list, which details the car’s exact configuration to 2019 model year specification, is summarised over five pages and is available to view on file. The Lamborghini was built in right-hand drive and delivered new in the United Kingdom, where it was registered for the road on 24 October 2018., The consigning owner acquired the Aventador via main dealer Lamborghini Chelmsford in September 2020, with the odometer reading noted at that time around 600 miles. description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Some of the most beautiful bodies on the early Derby Bentley chassis were produced not in England, but in Brussels by the renowned Belgian firm, Vesters et Neirinck. Vesters et Neirinck enjoyed a close relationship with Rolls-Royce and Bentley during this era, courtesy of local dealer André Pisart, whose premises were only a short distance from the coachbuilder’s, and who, in collaboration with his wealthy clientele, spurred some remarkable creations into being., Among them was this 3½-Litre, chassis number B114DG, commissioned by Pisart on behalf of his client Claude Lang, a young Brussels financier. An especially beautiful fixed head coupé, the car featured a low raked windscreen, a rather crisp ‘blind-quarter’ roofline with a small formal rear window providing privacy to the four-passenger interior, and tapered pontoon fenders, in the front flanking a bonnet whose louvres extended into the scuttle, and in the rear enclosing a luggage compartment with a rack for additional cases. All was set off by judicious touches of bright metal and chrome, as well as full bare metal wheel covers. The result was an exceptionally pleasing design, that pleased Monsieur Lang most of all; he went on to commission a second Bentley two years later, on the 4¼-Litre chassis, that aped much of B114DG’s lines., B114DG was sold by Lang in the late prewar era to Armand Kirschen; Lang seems to have missed his prize, however, as he reacquired the car postwar, before finally selling it again, for the second and final time, in 1952 to Jan Verswyver of Antwerp. It eventually journeyed to England, probably for the first time as an intact automobile, and in the early 1980s was acquired by the well-known Roberts Family Collection of Rolls-Royces and Bentleys in Wales. The 3½-Litre remained in their care for some 40 years, before joining the distinguished collection of sporting automobiles from which it is now offered., With its matching 4¼-Litre now tucked away for good in the renowned Loh Collection, this is a singular opportunity to acquire an especially significant Derby Bentley, among the most truly beautiful of the “Silent Sports Cars”, with lines difficult to match and provenance as rich as its curves.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The 3½-Litre Bentley was introduced to the public at the Ascot Racecourse in August 1933. To limit re-tooling costs, it was based on the Rolls-Royce 20/25 HP chassis. The new Bentley engine was reconfigured from the 20/25’s 2¾-litre motor by increasing displacement and adding a new cross-flow head, twin SU carburettors, a higher compression ratio, and a re-profiled camshaft. The result was a fast, smooth, long-lasting, responsive, and excellent-handling car that was marketed as “The Silent Sports Car”. Well-received by the press and public alike, 1,191 were sold between 1933 and 1937., Chassis number B169AE was bodied by Barker & Company, the revered London coachbuilder long favoured by royalty, as an all-weather tourer of unusually sporting design. It featured cycle-style front wings, curved running boards that hugged against the frame rails, a rather low windscreen, and a single rear-mounted spare with metal cover, reminiscent of that seen on the famous ‘Owen’ Phantom II Continentals. Unusually, the radiator, headlights, and other frontal brightwork were all specified to be finished in ‘heavy silver plate!’ The finished motorcar was supplied in April 1934 to longstanding Rolls-Royce and Bentley customer Arthur Gibbs of Bramley, Surrey. It remained in his ownership until 1939, then was acquired by the Rt Hon Viscount Mountgarret, with his address listed as the family seat, Nidd Hall in North Yorkshire, now a Grade II listed building and hotel., A subsequent owner acquired the car with the intention of enjoying it in long-distance rallies, and reportedly undertook a considerable sum in preparing the car for events such as the 2017 Kyoto-Tokyo Rally. It was also awarded Best of Class at the Salon Privé Concours at Blenheim Palace in 2019. Since being acquired by the present caretaker, a longtime Bentley enthusiast, it has remained well-kept in his ownership. Accompanied by copies of its build records from the Rolls-Royce Enthusiasts’ Club, it would be eligible for any number of most enjoyable rallies and showings in new ownership, as one of the most attractive 3½-Litres available.
