PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Ferrari kept its head when all about them were losing theirs during the 2008 Formula 1 World Championship season. McLaren was still reeling from the fallout of the infamous ‘Spygate’ scandal and bitter 2007 rivalry between former team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso; Renault would instruct Nelson Piquet Jr to deliberately crash out of the 2008 Singapore Grand Prix. Amid the turmoil, defending Drivers’ champion Kimi Räikkönen and Felipe Massa delivered Ferrari its record-extending 16th Constructors’ crown., Almost two decades later, still no other team comes close to matching that feat. The next-most decorated outfit, McLaren, boasts 10 teams’ titles by comparison. Even Ferrari itself is yet to add to the tally. Recognising the scale of the achievement at the time, Ferrari saw fit to christen the convertible counterpart to its harder-edged 430 Scuderia model the “16M”., Like the coupé, it housed a mid-mounted naturally aspirated 4.3-litre V-8 engine that delivered 503 brake horsepower via the F1-SuperFast2 six-speed transmission. Despite featuring significant strengthening and stiffening of the open body, Ferrari engineers nonetheless managed to slash 80 kilograms from the kerb weight of the F430 Spider thanks to a crash diet that included lightened front and rear bumpers, forged alloy wheels exclusive to the model, and re-worked front suspension and steering. As a sign of just how committed engineers were to weight saving, even the wheel bolts were reproduced in titanium., From the stated production run of 499 examples, the car offered here was supplied new to the United Kingdom configured in right-hand-drive form. Compared to many red and black Scuderia Spider 16Ms, it stands out courtesy of its bright Bianco Avus bodywork with racing stripe and red soft-top roof over a special-order red leather interior. Further details include the carbon fibre interior trim and white tachometer plus wing-mounted exterior Ferrari shields., Recorded in the accompanying service book, the Scuderia Spider 16M was delivered on 10 October 2009 via Graypaul Nottingham to its first owner in Lincolnshire. A further stamp in the service book shows a return to the official Ferrari franchise for maintenance in October 2011. Under the care of a new owner in Wales and as part of its ongoing maintenance by marque dealers and specialists, the car was entrusted to Dick Lovett Swindon for its annual servicing between January 2012 and July 2016., Purchased by the previous owner in March 2018, the Scuderia Spider 16M was cared for by H R Owen in Cheltenham and DK Engineering. Notable work carried out, as supported by the numerous invoices that are available to view on file, includes DK Engineering replacing the front lower ball joints and track rod ends in May 2018., The Ferrari was acquired by the vendor in June 2024. Sparingly driven in their possession, it displayed 13,150 miles on the odometer at the time of cataloguing. The Scuderia Spider 16M is offered with its owner’s guides in their leather folio further to the tool and tyre inflator kits., With reports that as few as 48 examples of the Scuderia Spider 16M were configured in right-hand drive, this UK-supplied car—offered in a lesser-spotted colour scheme and boasting Ferrari main dealer and specialist maintenance history—is sure to appeal to Prancing Horse aficionados.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: One of the great entrepreneurs and impresarios of the early French automobile industry, Adolphe Clément had his initial success racing bicycles, moving into their sale and manufacturer in 1895. The following year his firm merged with that of fellow pioneer Alexandre Darracq, and in 1897 introduced its first motor vehicle, then known as the Clément-Panhard. By 1901 the firm was producing a four-cylinder model, modernised further the following year with overhead intake valves and producing some 16 horsepower. The result was one of the most powerful and sophisticated British motorcars of the Veteran age, known for the superb quality of its engineering., According to a 1934 description in that year’s London to Brighton Veteran Car Run programme, this particular 12/16 HP Clément was originally delivered in its home country but moved across the Channel in early 1905. It was stored for nearly a quarter of a century in the owner’s coach house until its acquisition in 1933 by one A R Utley, passing soon after to noted early British collector A W F Smith. Wearing the Manchester registration “N1261”, apparently issued upon its arrival in England, the car was campaigned in its well-preserved original condition by Smith on the Run until 1938, then postwar in 1946, and again from 1947 through 1956. In 1948 it was officially dated as a 1903 model by the Veteran Car Club of Great Britain, with the Certificate on file., Described as still being very original down to its paint, the car was sold at the dispersal of the Smith stable in 1968 to renowned collector Neil Corner, who himself drove it on that year’s Run. It was eventually transacted by Corner to A M ‘Tony’ Goodman, then in 1977 to prominent American collector Barry Hon. Mr Hon maintained the car for some years in England, occasionally exercising it on the Run. He had a new crankshaft installed in addition to other mechanical works such as the fitment of disc brakes, in the 1980s and 1990s. In the early 2000s it was brought to California and restored by the noted Tired Iron Works of Monrovia, after which it was shown at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance in 2006., Acquired by the present owner from the Hon collection in 2015, the Clément has undergone much mechanical sorting. This includes the fitment of a 12-volt electrical system with alternator and LED lights, for reliability and safety in use on future Runs, with invoices for works through 2023 included in the file. The result is a delightful machine in every regard, with fine build quality, an excellent restoration, and rich heritage with some of the most prominent Veteran motorcar enthusiasts on both sides of the Atlantic.

sale_title: 1936 Leyland Cub London Transport Interstation Bus
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The unusual design of this 1936 Leyland Cub Interstation bus was dictated by its very specific use case: the nighttime transportation of passengers, and their belongings, between the major railway stations and termini of London. The rear half of the bus contained a hold for luggage, much of which would have been in the bulky travelling cases of the era, with additional seating above; hence, the unique “semi-decker” configuration that readily distinguished the Interstation from more typical mass-transit equipment. Fares for this special service were, according to an October 1936 article in, , ‘a shilling for adults and sixpence for children in each direction between any two main line stations’., The accompanying original registration booklet for the bus offered here notes that it was first registered on 1 October of 1936, which marked the beginning of Interstation service. The buses were repurposed during wartime, with this example being used by the ENSA performing arts group to provide entertainment to armed forces personnel but returned to Interstation use following the conclusion of hostilities and remained in operation until late 1950., In 1953, the bus was registered by the London Fire Brigade, which is understood to have used it for personnel transport. By June 1961, it had entered private ownership, and was registered to a Mr Raymond Ernest Ruberry of Surrey. It was in the care of a new owner, Mr Alan Brian Cross of Sussex, by July 1968., Under current ownership, the bus underwent a multi-year cosmetic and mechanical refurbishment carried out by Historic Vehicle Restoration Ltd of Byfleet. Completed in early 2021, this restoration returned the Leyland to its pre-war glory, including its distinctive blue and light-yellow livery complete with London Transport Inter Station gold leaf lettering. In November 2023 the bus completed the Historic Commercial Vehicle Society (HCVS) London to Brighton Run, and it has also been a participant in select gatherings and bus shows., Attractively and correctly restored, this rare surviving Leyland Cub Interstation is an eye-catching, and distinctive, alternative to the more commonly seen double-decker buses of its era. It is offered from the estate of a well-known member of the HCVS and would no doubt be happily welcomed to any number of rallies and exhibitions in the future.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The early motoring world was one of characters and scoundrels. Harry J Lawson was both; he sought to monopolise motorcar manufacturing in Britain by buying up the patents to essentially all necessary components and designs. He would be stymied by the courts, but his year-old Great Horseless Carriage Company survived by reorganising in 1898 as the Motor Manufacturing Company. MMC, as it became more widely known, initially built automobiles of Daimler design—appropriate, as they shared Coventry’s famed Motor Mills with Daimler’s British arm., MMC eventually evolved its models, relocated to another Coventry location, and continued in fits and starts until 1908, when a final move to London proved the company’s killing blow. MMC left behind a handful of well-built automobiles, solidly engineered in the tradition of its Daimler origins, and much-enjoyed by those fortunate enough to own them today., The 8 HP MMC offered here has had its ownership history traced back to a W F Parr of The Broadway Garage in Harrow Weald, Middlesex, with whom it had apparently been stored since 1909, fitted with unusual later coachwork. It was subsequently sold to a Mr Broard, then by him in 1955 to Stanley Gilks, a motorcycle dealer in Ickenham, Middlesex, by which time it had been disassembled for restoration. Mr Gilks’s son, Geoffrey, undertook a restoration completed around 1960, after which the car was used in several events and supplied for the production of two films, the 1965 classic, and 1967’s, . Although later restoration work was undertaken in the 1980s, the car was not widely used after its movies appearances, while remaining in the care of the Gilks family until its acquisition by the present owner in 2015. Long represented as a 1904, it is noted in the 2002 Veteran Car Club Members Handbook, in the Gilks’s ownership, as being a 1902., A most charming Veteran motorcar of interesting, well-known history and solid, practical design, this MMC has much to recommend it to the connoisseur of the earliest era of motoring.

sale_title: 1931 Invicta 4½-Litre S-Type ‘Low Chassis’ Sports by Vanden Plas
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Especially when lined up alongside contemporary Bentleys, the low-slung nature of the Invicta S-Type is immediately apparent. A mere 77 examples of the British sports car were reportedly built, with chassis number S40 completed in March 1931 wearing Vanden Plas “Sports 4-seater” bodywork. Entries in the famed coachbuilder’s order book indicate that Vanden Plas would dress just 19 Invictas, with only 11 being S-Types., Finished identically to the S-Type exhibited at the 1930 British Motor Show (the Vanden Plas order book reads: “as show model”), chassis S40 was first registered for road use on 13 March 1931. It was assigned the registration number “WD 2024”, as the car wears at the time of auction. The first owner, Mr John Harry Ansell, who would later own a second low-chassis Invicta, purchased the car via Birmingham dealership Flewitt Ltd. Come 1938, the S-Type was registered to Clifford Motors in Southampton., Between 1940 and 1942, chassis S40 belonged to Sub-Lieutenant T Thistlewaite—most likely Tom ‘Scrap’ Thistlewaite, who raced for the Works Bentley team in the 1926 edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans. A new owner took possession in June 1942, but only for two months before selling it to noted collector George Edward Milligen. According to Milligen, he came to buy the Invicta so swiftly because the seller had escaped police pursuit by taking up residency aboard a yacht in Malta., Milligen had the Invcita repainted in RAF Blue and would, over the next six decades of ownership, cover more than 50,000 miles in chassis S40. Under his meticulous care, the car was submitted in 1955 to The Laystall Motor Engineering Works for a rebuild of the 4.5-litre Meadows six-cylinder engine, boosting output from 126 to a fine 141 brake horsepower., Following Milligen’s death in 2004, his collection was disbanded. The Invicta was bought by The Fighter Collection, based at Duxford Aerodrome, before being sent to vintage racing car expert Blakeney Motorsport for a mechanical overhaul in 2010. Rebuilding the SU carburettors, water pump, front axle, brakes, and propshaft meant the S-Type was ready for Patrick Blakeney-Edwards to drive chassis S40 up the Prescott hill climb with the Vintage Sports-Car Club later that year., Acquired by the vendor, a member of The Invicta Car Club, chassis S40 was taken to Setford and Company for a body-off restoration carried out between May 2017 and January 2020. The car was checked over and the original ‘Sanction 0’ Meadows engine—fitted with small main bearing caps, a unique camshaft drive, and starter motor—was rebuilt with a new crankshaft, rods, and pistons. This S-Type now features closer gear ratios plus a high-ratio touring crown wheel and pinion axle, while the suspension was refreshed in line with original specification using photographs in the history file that date back to the late 1940s. Furthermore, a chronometric clock, sourced from a Bristol Blenheim light bomber, was added to aid with timing on long-distance driving tours. Once completed, the corresponding VSCC Eligibility Document was issued on 8 November 2018, Chassis S40 would go on to be displayed at the Heveningham Hall Concours in September 2019, raced one at Donington Park, and has been driven extensively across mainland Europe. As such, the Invicta would make for a brilliant companion for continental journeys cruising at motorway speeds, in addition to being eligible for ongoing participation in numerous prestigious concours and race events., Finished in RAF Blue with a red coachline to match the red leather upholstery, the Invicta is supplied with a tonneau cover and—in addition to myriad invoices and the VSCC Eligibility Document—the sizeable history file is supported by eight MoT certificates dating back to April 1964 and a period “buff” logbook. The car is also accompanied by a selection of original components, although the vendor notes that these are unserviceable (for more information, please speak to an RM Sotheby’s Specialist)., Boasting a compelling life story, including ownership by a ‘Bentley Boy’ and 60 years with George Milligen, chassis S40 deserves special attention even among the small pool of surviving Invicta 4½-Litre S-Types. This highly desirable pre-war sports car would therefore make for a rare, fascinating, and versatile entry into any stable of vintage automobiles.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of reportedly only 77 examples of the low-chassis Invicta S-Type built, Completed in March 1931; one of just 11 cars to feature Vanden Plas coachwork, Retained for six decades by George Milligen; other notable owners include Bentley Works driver Tom Thistlewaite and The Flying Collection at Duxford, Body-off rebuild completed by Setford and Company between May 2017 and January 2020; accompanying invoices total nearly £85,000, Eligible for concours and race events, with VSCC Eligibility Document issued in November 2018; ideally suited for long-distance driving tours, Supplied with tonneau cover, selection of original used components, and substantial history file with MoT certificates, period “buff” logbook, and photographs dating from the late 1940s

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Featuring remarkably original condition highlighted by the presence of its matching-numbers engine and body, this charming early 190 SL is one of the finest examples to be presented at auction in recent times. According to a build record copy on file, chassis number 00435 was finished in black paint over a red leather interior, and the car was dispatched to the Packard/Mercedes-Benz Distributor in New York in early September 1955., A signed statement from the widow of the second owner clarifies that this Mercedes-Benz was sold new in 1955 to Ted Kangie, a manager of the US Steel plant in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Mr Kangie was apparently told that his car was only the second example imported to the United States. While this may be apocryphal, production details such as the single sun visor and door-mounted mirrors prove that the SL is certainly one of the earlier examples built., Mr Kangie was soon transferred to the US Steel plant in Gary, Indiana, and the 190 SL faithfully accompanied him to a new residence in nearby Ogden Dunes. When he later decided to move to Florida, Mr Kangie sold the car in 1969 to an admiring friend and neighbour, Robert Charles Bills, who was a member of the Chicago-area Mercedes-Benz Club., As revealed by service invoices spanning from September 1969 to May 1993, Mr Bills took great care of the Mercedes-Benz, fastidiously replacing minor parts to ensure good operating condition. In 1989 Mr Bills relocated to Lake Tawakoni, Texas, and the 190 SL was soon put into storage at its new Texas home., In October 2007, the owner sold the car to an ex-Mercedes-Benz mechanic named Don Tremelling. Mr Tremelling recommissioned the SL for road use with a gradual sympathetic freshening, sourcing parts from Mercedes-Benz Classic, and locating an original factory hard top in complementary red. His efforts yielded an award for the car at the 2013 Keels & Wheels Concours d’Elegance., In October 2013 Mr Tremelling offered the Mercedes-Benz at RM Auctions’ Hershey sale, and it was acquired then by the present keeper, a UK-based collector. Since then, the car has been carefully stored, used sparingly, and maintained in good mechanical running order, with strict discipline to preserve its unmolested factory specification and charming patina (invoices available for workshop visits)., This honestly presented 190 SL is one of the most original examples to ever pass through RM Sotheby’s purview. sale_title: 1956 Bentley S1 Continental Drophead Coupé by Park Ward
description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Unlike the majority of Bentley drophead coupés produced in the post-war era, Park Ward’s body style number 700 for the S1 Continental was not an “adaptation” from factory saloon stampings. Rather, it was a fully custom body, built from the ground up in aluminium by the revered coachbuilder on the exceptionally rigid, magnificently well-tuned Continental chassis, a renowned “gentleman’s express” of the period., The picture of well-considered grace, John Blatchley’s lines were a classic from the moment they were first carried out and have long been considered one of the peaks of modern Bentley styling. Distinguishing the design were smooth and subtle curves—long, fully “flow through” wings reached gracefully from the front to the rear, with a subtle kick-up forming “hips” over the back wheels, and the very tiniest vestige of tailfins at their trailing tips. Significantly, thanks to its alloy panelling, this model also ensured maximum performance from the chassis beneath., Only 94 Drophead Coupés were produced on the S1 Continental chassis, for an eager clientele of the most sophisticated motoring enthusiasts on both sides of the Atlantic—captains of industry, Hollywood stars, and world royalty among them. Today, the heirs to that tradition happily maintain the restored survivors., Chassis number BC33BG, offered here, was one of 58 right-hand-drive Drophead Coupés built to style number 700. It was specified with the later high-compression engine fed by larger carburettors, as well as an automatic gearbox and power-assisted steering. It was originally delivered to Alfred James McAlpine. Chairman of the Northeast England civil engineering firm Sir Alfred McAlpine & Sons, he was a prominent vintage automobile collector and member of a family that had been avid Rolls-Royce and Bentley clients for some 40 years., The current owner’s father acquired the Bentley in Australia in 1979. He retained it until his passing in 1992, when it was inherited by the vendor. It was used by the consigning owner regularly for over a quarter of a century, still in its very original condition, while maintaining it properly. Thus, it remained in fine, largely original condition when it finally came time for restoration, undertaken by revered firm P&A Wood and completed in time for the 2023 Pebble Beach Concours., The fastidious, body-off, and ground-up restoration was initially overseen by Paul and Andrew Wood themselves; later by Paul’s daughters, Georgina and Louise Wood. Undergoing a full engine and mechanical rebuild, the car was finished in a spectacular combination of Shell Grey over Astral Blue, with Navy Blue hides and blue hood, and incorporated air conditioning for comfortable long-distance touring. The result is one of the most beautiful-yet-practical Bentley convertibles of its type., Freshly completed, the S1 Continental reappeared at the 2023 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, achieving 2nd in the hotly contested Postwar British Luxury class. It went on to be awarded at the Rolls-Royce Enthusiasts Club meeting in England in 2024. The S1 has since remained in the same good hands that have now cared for it, within one loving family both before and after an exquisite restoration, for the last 47 years. Accompanying the car is an impressive history and restoration book, detailing its past as well as the authenticity involved in its restoration in exhaustive detail. The S1 is further offered with its original owner’s manual books., Offered ready for continued show appearances on either side of the Atlantic, chassis BC33BG is an utterly superb example of a truly classic design, representing one of the finest works on the S1 Continental—among the best grand tourers of its own or any age.

LOT_SUMMARY: Offered from 47 years of loving, enthusiast family ownership, Superbly restored by noted firm P&A Wood, Class award-winner at the 2023 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance; winner of its class at the Rolls-Royce Enthusiasts Club Annual Rally in 2024, One of 58 right-hand-drive Drophead Coupés to style number 700, with fully custom aluminium coachwork, Originally delivered to noted motoring enthusiast Alfred James McAlpine, Among the most superb survivors of a highly regarded design on an exceptional chassis

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: After applying its revered GTO moniker to the high-performance version of the 599 GTB, Ferrari chose to revive another legendary name from its past for the track-focused development of the F12berlinetta: Tour de France. The nickname was originally given to the 250 GT Berlinetta Competizione in the late 1950s after its stunning streak of wins in the Tour de France Automobile, an endurance race held on French roads from 1899 to 1986., First unveiled in 2015, the Ferrari F12tdf was the most powerful naturally aspirated production Ferrari to date, featuring a 6.3-litre V-12 tuned to develop 769 horsepower. Its space-frame chassis, co-developed with Carrozzeria Scaglietti, was comprised of 12 different alloys, resulting in a frame 20 per cent stiffer than the preceding 599’s yet more than 60 kilograms lighter. Extensive use of carbon fibre reduced the car’s weight by an additional 110 kilograms versus the F12berlinetta., The F12tdf also boasted numerous improvements over the already technologically advanced F12berlinetta. A seven-speed, dual-clutch, paddle-shift transmission offered shorter ratios and quicker gear changes, while carbon-ceramic disc brakes from the LaFerrari were specified with single-piece callipers. Notably, the F12tdf was also the first Ferrari to feature four-wheel steering as standard., The F12tdf’s larger front splitter and rear diffuser, deeper side sills, and additional vents, including the distinctive “Aerobridge” on the front flanks (which directs airflow along the sides of the car), all combine to improve aerodynamics and create a far more aggressive visual profile. A taller rear spoiler and “active” rear diffuser helped achieve 87 per cent more downforce compared with the standard F12berlinetta. Sprinting from zero to 62 mph in 2.9 seconds before reaching a top speed of 211 mph, the F12tdf could blaze through a lap of Ferrari’s Fiorano test track just 1.3 seconds behind the flagship LaFerrari., In recognition of how special the F12tdf was, Ferrari capped production at 799 cars, and each example is appointed with a special commemorative interior plaque reading “Limited Edition – 1\799”.  With guaranteed exclusivity and such a dazzling technical profile, the F12tdf became an instant collectable, attracting the admiration of supercar aficionados and Ferrari purists alike., As clarified by a special plaque, the livery of the featured F12tdf was inspired by chassis number 0563 GT, an early example of the first-series 250 GT Berlinetta Tour de France. Officially finished in Azzurro La Plata paint with a longitudinal French tri-colour racing stripe, chassis number 227277 was upholstered in Alcantara Charcoal (including the boot carpet, boot trim, seats inner trim, headliner, and centre console) with complementary tri-colour racing stripes on the seats., The, was desirably specified with a suspension lifter, sports exhaust, and red-painted brake callipers, while carbon fibre was used on a host of elements, including the fog lamps, dashboard inserts, under-door covers, rear bench trim, and hub caps. The spirit of Maranello was imbued with Scuderia Ferrari shields on the wings, and stitched Cavallino Rampante motifs on the headrests., Configured in right-hand drive for allocation to the United Kingdom, the Ferrari was first registered in May 2017. Invoices on file clarify that by March 2022 the F12tdf was being tended by DK Engineering, one of the country’s foremost Ferrari specialists. From 2022 to March 2024 the car also received occasional attention as needed by the marque dealer HR Owen, including annual services in March 2022 and 2024., Following four brief ownerships that involved very little driving, the Ferrari was acquired by the consigning owner in December 2024. The F12tdf continues to benefit from a life of mild driving use, exemplified by the current remarkably low odometer reading of just 3,195 miles at the time of cataloguing., The original Tour de France Automobile race rewarded cars that combined maximum performance with drivability. The F12tdf is, appropriately, the ultimate expression of the concept—an extreme road car that is equally at home on the track. This superb, minimally driven example makes a stunning impression with its unique livery of Azzurro La Plata over Charcoal, matching its uber-athletic performance with an elegantly tasteful cosmetic ode to its namesake road rally., Accompanied by the owner’s manual and reference guides in the proper pouch, this exquisitely finished and rare Ferrari would make a sensational crowning addition to any stable of Prancing Horses. Chassis number 227277 is sure to provide the next caretaker with the considerable thrills of its outrageous performance envelope and top-shelf rarity, as one of the Italian marque’s most special limited edition models.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of 799 examples built; the ultimate evolution of the F12berlinetta, Displayed just 3,195 miles at the time of cataloguing, Beautifully finished in Azzurro La Plata with French tri-colour racing stripes over an Alcantara Charcoal interior, Documented with service invoices, prior UK V5C registrations, and MoT test certificates, A minimally driven and exceptionally presented example of one of Ferrari’s most compelling modern limited edition models

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: This Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Roadster holds a truly fascinating origin story, which has been extensively researched with support from the factory. Out of just 26 examples built in 1963, chassis number 198.042.10.003257 offered here was specified with White (DB 050) paintwork over a Red (DB 203) leather interior. As one of the final 209 Roadsters made, it was fitted with the coveted alloy-block engine and supplied with disc brakes. Completed on 7 February 1963, this is the penultimate 300 SL to roll off the production line, with chassis 003258 bringing the illustrious W198 lifecycle to an end the very next day., Whereas that final car found a private buyer the same month, this Roadster landed in Austria to be sold by a Mercedes-Benz dealership in Salzburg. However, after 10 months, it had yet to tempt an owner—likely an outcome of the new and considerably less expensive W113 SL having arrived. As a result, the car returned to Stuttgart in November to be converted for the North American market. The subsequent fitment of sealed-beam headlights, instruments that read in miles, a Becker Grand Prix radio, and whitewall tyres means this car is documented with two factory data cards. Notably, the car kept its European-specification 3.64 rear axle., Finally, accompanied by a hardtop roof, the car was collected by its first owner in the United States on 14 February 1964, more than a year after its original production date. Just three out of all 1,858 Roadsters completed were invoiced to 1964, making it among the final 300 SLs sold. Per correspondence in the history file between 300 SL historian Dr Frank Spellman and Daimler-Benz Classic, chassis 003207 was released similarly late on its way to the Shah of Iran, and at least one further car is known to have been delivered in 1965., Concluding the protracted search for a custodian, the first known owner of this Mercedes-Benz is one Mr Robert Lindsay—as evidenced in the history file by a 22 September 1967 invoice from British Motor Cars of Spokane, Washington, when the odometer was noted with 19,050 miles. The following January, just 315 miles later, Mr Lindsay returned to BMC to have a new engine block and pistons fitted. It is believed that the replacement unit was an unstamped spare from the factory, as was common practice for the less proven and more fragile alloy 3.0-litre M198 straight-six., Mr Lindsay retained ownership through to late 1970, before the 300 SL Roadster was bought by Mr Bill Sutherland of the Sutherland-Marlow Mercedes-Benz concern in Spokane. Prior to selling the car at the end of the following year, he had covered nigh on 10,000 miles. A final 24 November 1971 service receipt from his custodianship logged the odometer at 28,547 miles. From December, chassis 003257 was retained by fellow marque dealer Mr Phil Smart Sr of Seattle., A vehicle valuation report dated 22 April 1987 still listed Mr Smart Sr as the owner of the 300 SL, at which time it was noted at 33,000 miles. Then, according to the Gull Wing Group International’s, , this car was purchased by renowned collector Mr Gordon Apker. Reportedly, come 1988, he was contacted by a Mr David Brice. At a time when Roadster values had barely crept above $100,000, the Australian investor offered a colossal $500,000. Naturally, chassis 003257 had found its new owner. In 1992, having already acquired Mr Brice’s alloy-bodied Gullwing, legendary 300 SL collector Mr Thomas Taffet of Chatsworth, California bought this matching-specification White over Red convertible. Three years on, he sold the Roadster to a German collector., At the turn of the new millennium, Phil Smart Jr had tracked down his father’s former 300 SL and bought it back into the family in Seattle. In 2001, he tasked marque specialist Rudi Konicezk of Rudi & Company in Victoria, British Columbia with a bare-metal respray. Newly resplendent in its factory colour combination, the car was gifted back to Smart Sr., The father-and-son duo retained possession for a further 14 years. During this time, the Mercedes-Benz made several appearances at the Kirkland Concours d’Elegance. A rosette was awarded when the Roadster claimed 2nd in its class in September 2013, as chassis 003257 marked its 50th anniversary. Subsequently acquired by a prominent collector in California, who kept the car for five years, the 300 SL Roadster was imported to the United Kingdom in 2020 by its consigning owner., In 2024, the Roadster was sent to 300 SL specialist Martin Cushway of Sudbury, Suffolk. A comprehensive service, including the fitment of a new timing chain and refurbishment of the rear axle, was completed as part of work exceeding £20,000. At this time, Cushway inspected the car and recorded it as having retained its original chassis, body, gearbox, rear axle, plus left and right kingpins. Meanwhile, the unstamped replacement engine (dated 7 October 1965 on the block) sports a tag bearing the car’s original engine number (198.982.10.000218), and Cushway states that the camshaft and cylinder head appear to be original., Accompanied by a Mercedes-Benz Classic Certificate issued in April 2007, this fantastic and significant 300 SL Roadster is further complemented by its factory hardtop roof, owner’s guides in their folio, and a two-piece fitted luggage set for the boot. Also supplied with the car is the history file, comprising of three folders, as well as a Gull Wing Group technical folio, workshop manual, a tool kit, jack, plus spare wheel., Regarded by many as the original supercar, the W198 is extremely desirable in any form. The Roadster model, introduced in 1957, then improved upon the breed. Of the convertibles, it is the later examples to feature an alloy-block engine and disc brakes that are most coveted among collectors. Chassis 003257 offers all those immensely appealing traits in addition to being an extremely rare example of a beautifully preserved 300 SL. More than that, it is this car’s standing as the penultimate Roadster built and its incredibly late delivery date that must surely rank it as one of the most exceptional 300 SLs on the planet.

LOT_SUMMARY: The penultimate 300 SL Roadster built; one of only three delivered in 1964, Rare and highly desirable specification; alloy engine and disc brake example, Beautifully preserved; presents in fantastically original condition, Retains its matching-numbers chassis, body, gearbox, kingpins, and rear axle, Wears its factory-correct colours of White over the original Red leather interior, Accompanied by factory hardtop roof, owner’s guides folio, and two-piece fitted luggage set, Documented by a comprehensive history file with invoices dating back to 1967, Mercedes-Benz Classic Certificate, and copies of the factory data cards

The model marked the long-awaited return of a front-engined V-12 grand tourer in the range, was conceived during the marque’s vaunted Luca di Montezemolo era, and boasted a six-speed open-gate manual transmission in addition to easy-on-the-eye styling by Pininfarina., The example presented here offers what is quite possibly the very best configuration for the 550 Maranello. description_block:
PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: In 1995, McLaren joined forced with Mercedes-Benz in Formula 1. The successful partnership yielded back-to-back Drivers’ Championships for Mika Häkkinen in 1998 and 1999, while he and team-mate David Coulthard combined to secure the 1998 Constructors’ title. The alliance remained competitive throughout the 2000s, providing a launchpad for Lewis Hamilton to make his topflight debut in 2007. He chalked his first Drivers’ crown the following season., To celebrate their F1 success, Mercedes-Benz and McLaren co-developed a road car. After the Vision SLR concept debuted at the 1999 North American International Auto Show in Detroit, the well-received prototype eventually transitioned into a full production model, revealed at the Frankfurt Motor Show in September 2003. Officially designated the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren, the supercar was assembled at McLaren’s state-of-the-art facility in Woking., The SLR McLaren featured a stunning design with a lightweight carbon fibre tub and dihedral doors. Initially offered only as a coupé, a roadster variant joined the lineup in 2007. Performance was breathtaking, courtesy of a 617-horsepower, supercharged 5.4-litre V-8. At McLaren’s insistence the engine was mounted behind the front axle, giving the car a front-mid-engine layout. Power was sent to the rear wheels via a five-speed AMG Speedshift R Automatic gearbox featuring three driving modes: Comfort, Sport, and Manual—the latter utilising steering wheel-mounted paddle shifters. The SLR McLaren launched from 0 to 60 mph in just 3.8 seconds before hitting 207 mph., Special editions of the SLR McLaren were produced, including 300 examples of the 722 (150 coupés, 150 roadsters), 75 examples of the Stirling Moss, and just 12 SLR HDK coupés converted by McLaren Special Operations (MSO). But the rarest street-legal variant is the ‘McLaren Edition’ by MSO. Only 25 were built, of which just four were Roadsters., The McLaren Edition offered SLR owners an ultra-exclusive opportunity to send their car back to the factory for a bespoke upgrade package. This conversion included improved aerodynamics and handling, weight reduction, plus custom exterior and interior finishes if desired., This 2007 McLaren Edition started life as a standard SLR McLaren Roadster finished in Crystal Laurit Silver Metallic over Anthracite. It was ordered for the Great Britian and Northern Ireland market and specified in left-hand drive. In January 2009, the car was sent to MSO to be upgraded to ‘722 S’ style. This included a repaint in Alabaster White, with 722 Edition features installed—namely, the aerodynamic package, tinted lights, 722S wheels with McLaren logo centre caps, and an interior retrim featuring comfort seats and carbon kick plates. Per the invoice on file from MSO, the total cost exceeded £78,000. This SLR was the first of its kind to be modified by MSO, and these initial changes pre-dated the finalised ‘McLaren Edition’ programme that was later offered., Following a conversation with the original owner and then MSO director Harold Dermot, a decision was made to modify the car further and create what came to be known as the ‘McLaren Edition’. In 2010, the car returned to Woking for further MSO upgrades. The body was painted in its current colour of Midas Fire Grey, featuring revised front and rear bumpers, side panels, a Stirling Moss rear diffuser, and ducktail boot lid. This resulted in a 50-kilogram weight saving and a 20 per cent increase in downforce. The exterior gained carbon fibre mirrors, red-painted brake callipers with the McLaren logo, and front wheel arch vents. A special exhaust system was installed alongside modifications to the suspension. Inside, the seats were retrimmed in red leather and black Alcantara with red stitching and feature the McLaren logo. A carbon fibre steering wheel was fitted, with the final detail being a plaque denoting ‘001’. With the full conversion completed in late 2010, the MSO invoices on file total more than £120,000., With the project a resounding success, MSO offered this style of customer-oriented modifications to other owners. The firm went on to modify 25 SLRs, four of them being Roadsters. This SLR McLaren Edition has covered just 3,178 miles at time of cataloguing. It is accompanied by a battery tender, manuals with pouch, and stamped service book denoting Mercedes-Benz dealer services from 2008 to 2020. In 2023, a major service was carried out by SPS Automotive Performance in Germany, with the most recent service untaken in June 2026 by Mercedes-Benz of Belfast., In an era where the rarest configuration is most sought after, this example—McLaren Edition serial number 001—represents the pinnacle of the vaunted SLR McLaren line, and the car which kick-started the MSO programme. As one of just four roadsters upgraded to McLaren Edition specification, it is sure to attract the attention of discerning enthusiasts.

LOT_SUMMARY: The first McLaren Automotive-era car modified by McLaren Special Operations (MSO), kick-starting the revered department’s upgrade and customisation programme, The rarest road-legal special edition of the SLR McLaren; the first of 25 total ‘McLaren Edition’ examples produced by MSO and one of just four Roadsters, Finished in striking Midas Fire Grey over a McLaren red leather and black Alcantara interior, Sparingly driven; the odometer showed just 3,178 miles at the time of cataloguing, Accompanied by its leather folio, manuals, service book, and MSO conversion invoices

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Finished in Oxford Blue with beige upholstery, this Bentley R-Type Continental Fastback Sports Saloon was built in right-hand drive and sported a floor-change manual gearbox. Denoted by its “BC” chassis number prefix, it benefited from a higher-compression engine and stiffer chassis tuning—courtesy of an improved all-welded frame—from the factory., According to, by Rodney Steel, chassis number BC30C was sold new via Bristol Motors to Thomas Harvey Simmonds in London. Pre-delivery testing completed two weeks prior, the car was first registered for road use on 9 March 1954. Mr Simmonds retained possession for three years before selling the R-Type Continental to a G Elliot, with G I Waker buying the car the following year in 1958., Long-lasting ownership would arrive in 1959. F H Wrigley kept the car through to 1980, at which point it was purchased by S R Collins. Chassis BC30C’s first spell in the United Kingdom came to an end five years later. Through noted Bentley expert Charles Howard, the R-Type Continental was exported to the United States upon its acquisition by children’s toy industry magnate Mr Harvey Greenfield of East Hampton in New York., Sparingly driven across its two decades in the US, the car was bought by the consigning owner in 2004 and returned to the UK. Under their care, the R-Type Continental was submitted to classic car specialist Graeme Hunt Ltd in Battersea for a total restoration carried out over a two-year period. As part of the process, air conditioning was discretely installed, Sunburst walnut trim and electric window lifts were sourced, the suspension enhanced, and sports-style front seats trimmed in Spinney Beck leather fitted. For the cosmetic overhaul, the owner chose a darkened tint of Oxford Blue and requested rear wheel spats featuring Mavrolian wavelets. Please note: the original straight-six has at some point been replaced, reportedly with a 4.9-litre engine—an improvement offered by the factory from July 1954., Enjoyed ever since by the vendor, the Bentley has breezed through European driving tours. Now offered for sale at RM Sotheby’s London auction, this R-Type Continental is primed to effortlessly waft a new custodian away on long-distance adventures.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Volkswagen could reasonably lay claim to the “hot hatch” crown, as pioneers of the high-performance compact car. Before the Mark I Volkswagen Golf GTI began production in 1975, other manufacturers had trialled the formula for a beefed-up small car, yet it was the German marque to first find mass market acclaim. Over multiple generations, the Golf GTI has defined the sector and the three-letter abbreviation for Grand Tourer Injection has become a buzzword for hot hatch enthusiasts. Volkswagen moved the goalposts once more, however, when the Golf R32 was revealed for the 2003 model year., Every bit as sporting as the earlier GTI, the R32 took Volkswagen’s Golf to another level. Improving on the turbocharged 1.8-litre petrol motor found as standard in the Mark IV Golf GTI, the R32 deployed a 3.2-litre VR6 engine—fitted as the performance option in Audi’s flagship TT coupé and closely related to the same displacement mill that propelled Porsche’s first-generation Cayenne—rated by the Wolfsburg marque for 237 brake horsepower and a 0-62 mph time of only 6.6 seconds. The R32 paved the way for later Golf R and other factory-tuned versions, cementing the model’s status as the definitive hot hatch., This example is one of circa 2,000 Golf R32s made for the Mark IV platform delivered new to the United Kingdom in right-hand drive and three-door hatchback form. Completed by the factory on 5 September 2003, the car was finished in Deep Blue Pearlescent over a Flannel Grey interior notably upholstered in rare Alcantara fabric. The Golf R32 was specified with options including a CD changer and Cruise Control System (CCS); the car was also built with option code “S0T”, denoting its build slot towards the end of series production. A full list of options—in a report spanning five pages—can be viewed in the accompanying history file., On 4 October 2003, the Golf R32 was registered for the road in the United Kingdom, with its first and only owner residing in Kent. Remarkably, some 23 years later, the VW remains with its sole and consigning owner, who has driven the car for just 390 miles. The car has been retained in storage for much of this time and its only instance of an MoT inspection was when it passed with 375 miles on the odometer on 3 October 2006. Bidders should note that, as a result of the car’s long-term storage, it will need recommissioning prior to being driven on the road. Please contact an RM Sotheby’s Car Specialist for more information., Now offered out of storage with an odometer reading barely exceeding delivery miles, this rare and seldom-touched hot hatch presents the ideal opportunity for those who may have missed the Golf R32 first time around to acquire a “like new” example.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of circa 2,000 examples of the Mark IV Golf R32 delivered new to the United Kingdom, Single ownership from new and barely driven; odometer shows a mere 390 miles at the time of cataloguing, Powered by a 3.2-litre VR6 engine, rated for 237 brake horsepower with 0-62 mph achieved in only 6.6 seconds; paired with a six-speed manual gearbox, Haldex-managed 4MOTION technology delivers power to all four wheels for optimum traction, Finished in Deep Blue Pearlescent over a Flannel Grey and Black interior complete with “R” stitching and Alcantara upholstery, The ideal opportunity to sample a “like new” Golf R32 as it was originally intended

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Inspired by motorsport greatness, beautifully styled, exceedingly rare, and powered purely by internal combustion. The Daytona SP3 makes a compelling case to be considered the most desirable Ferrari of the 21st Century., The marque established its Icona limited series to offer closest clients a blend of modern drivetrains cloaked in retro-themed bodywork. After paying tribute to its open-top sportscars of the late 1940s and 1950s with the Monza SP1, and two-seater SP2, Ferrari used the third Icona creation to honour its mid-engined prototypes of the 1960s., Between 1960 and 1965, the Scuderia set a record in the 24 Hours of Le Mans by snaring six outright victories. Then Ford brought the hot streak to a halt with its GT40 the following year. But, in a show of strength, Ferrari started the 1967 sportscar season with a remarkable podium lockout in the 24 Hours of Daytona as the factory 330 P3/4 and 330 P4 led the North American Racing Team-entered 412P. The three cars crossing the line side-by-side was an unsubtle riposte to Ford’s photo finish at the Circuit de la Sarthe eight months earlier., Unveiled in 2022, the Daytona SP3 was named to celebrate Ferrari’s historic achievement at the American circuit. The most apparent design cues taken from motorsport past are the wrap-around windscreen, pronounced wheel arches, removable roof panel, prominent wing mirrors, and slatted rear bodywork that combine to create the SP3’s astonishing, clean silhouette. Not employing active aerodynamics, engineers focused on passive systems such as the “chimneys” that extract low-pressure air from the underbody. This helped make the SP3 the most passively aerodynamically efficient Ferrari ever produced at the time of its launch., The underpinnings are no less significant. The Daytona SP3 employs a derivation of the 65-degree V-12 used in the 812 Superfast and LaFerrari halo hybrid hypercar. Driving the rear wheels via a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission, the 6.5-litre engine launches the SP3 from 0 to 62 mph in just 2.85 seconds. With an output of 829 brake horsepower, the Daytona SP3 houses not only the most potent non-electrically assisted 12-cylinder engine in Ferrari road car history but, incredibly, even eclipses the might of its V-12 Can-Am and Formula 1 cars., The breathtaking Daytona SP3 offered here, chassis number 277499, was completed by the Maranello factory in left-hand-drive form in June 2022. As denoted by the special plaque—positioned on the carbon fibre monocoque between the two seats—that reads “Vettura Di Sviluppo”, it was a designated development car., This SP3 therefore holds the distinction of being specified by Ferrari. Perfectly showcasing the design, it was configured in the Extra Range colour of Giallo Triplo Strato—Italian for ‘triple-layer yellow’. The exterior is complemented by Rosso Ferrari leather upholstery—adorning the dashboard, large-size integrated seat cushions and backrests, while the headrests feature the Cavallino logo—and upper and lower Alcantara accents. Adding to the attraction: the removable hardtop roof panel, lower bodywork, and lid lip were selected in carbon fibre, Scuderia shields are airbrushed onto the doors, and red callipers chosen to sit behind the five-spoke 20-inch forged diamond wheels. Conveniences include Apple CarPlay, front and rear parking cameras, plus a suspension lift system., While the limited run of 600 stated customer examples of the Daytona SP3 were delivered to their proud new owners, chassis 277499 was instead retained by Ferrari SpA and registered in Italy. Set for a busy start to life in its prominent role as a factory press car, it was steered by Andrew Frankel for the October 2022 issue of, . Emerging from his test at the Circuit de la Sarthe in France, Frankel wrote: “I have never in my life been in a road car that has attracted so much attention, and for almost exclusively the right reasons… You could argue that cars like the SP3 are not to be taken terribly seriously. But am I glad it exists and even happier to have driven it? With every bone in my body.”, The Daytona also thrilled the American automotive media during drives by, (at Dutch Grand Prix host venue Zandvoort) and, (Belgian Formula 1 circuit Spa-Francorchamps). Then, having already cemented itself as a darling in print, the SP3 would earn it television break in series 33, episode five of, . Aired on primetime BBC One on 18 December 2022, the Ferrari featured in what currently stands as the final instalment of the famed motoring show., Chassis 277499 remained with Ferrari SpA through to March 2025, at which time it was purchased by the vendor—the first and only private owner—via H R Owen (Ferrari Hatfield) and registered for road use in the United Kingdom. The car heads to RM Sotheby’s London auction accompanied by its owner’s guides, ECC Certificate of Conformity, tool and tyre inflator kits, plus both the removable carbon fibre roof panel and its collapsable canvas setup. The odometer displayed 2,948 miles at the time of cataloguing., Built and specified in Ferrari’s own image and only ever driven by those chosen by the factory, chassis 277499 already touts a compelling backstory. Due to its outstanding provenance as a development vehicle, it will surely rank among the most collectible of Daytona SP3s in the fullness of time., So powerful that it made marque history, this development car was kept as part of Ferrari’s inner circle and boasts single private ownership thereafter. Presented in extraordinary three-coat Giallo paint, it is poised to shine no matter the quality of its star-studded company.

LOT_SUMMARY: Among the most publicised Daytona SP3s; reviewed on, and in, ,, , plus, Left-drive development car built in June 2022; retained by Ferrari SpA for press use, One private owner; purchased by the vendor in March 2025 and registered in the UK, Specified by the factory; stunning Extra Range Giallo Triplo Strato paintwork over a Rosso Ferrari interior, Features carbon fibre roof panel and lower bodywork plus airbrushed Scuderia shields, Supplied with owner’s guides, ECC Certificate of Conformity, fabric roof, plus tool and tyre inflator kits, The odometer displayed 2,948 miles from new at the time of cataloguing

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: The 599 GTB Fiorano redefined grand touring for Ferrari in the mid-2000s. Although the marque had already transitioned away from a mid-engine layout for its V-12 models, the 550 Maranello and its 575M successor were more genteel, long-legged continent cruisers., But there was no escaping the sporting credentials of the 599 GTB. Introduced in 2006, it gained a rev-happy heart from the flagship Enzo hypercar. Resting entirely behind the front axle line, the naturally aspirated F140C V-12 engine displayed 6.0 litres to generate 604 brake horsepower. That marked a colossal 100 brake horsepower leap over the 575M. All told, the 599 GTB could sprint from to 62 mph in 3.7 seconds before topping out at 205 mph., Recorded in a letter—which is available to view on file—from Tony Willis of The Maranello Concessionaires Archive, the example offered here was completed in right-hand-drive form on 27 November 2007. It was specified in the smart metallic tone of Grigio Titanio over an interior featuring Bordeaux hide with a matching-colour headliner and carpets., As part of a generous specification, electrically operated Daytona-style seats were selected alongside contrasting Nero piping, stitching, and leather rear shelf. The cabin benefitted from the carbon fibre driver zone with LED shift-indicator lights, a Giallo tachometer, and the fitment of a Bose Hi-Fi system. Equipped with front and rear parking sensors, the Ferrari also gained Rosso brake callipers, Scuderia wing shields, and polished Challenge wheels., Originally imported via Ferrari North Europe, this 599 GTB was sold new via marque dealer Charles Hurst in Belfast, Northern Ireland on 3 March 2008. It was acquired by a second owner the following month, prior to a third longer-term keeper enjoying the car for 14 years from June 2009., Purchased by the vendor in August 2023, the 599 GTB Fiorano displayed 24,392 miles at the time of cataloguing. It is offered for sale accompanied by its owner’s guides in their leather folio, Ferrari Vehicle Identification Passport, tool kit, and battery conditioner.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: At the 2019 Geneva International Motor Show, McLaren hosted a press conference that served as a statement of intent for the marque’s burgeoning and impressive product portfolio. Alongside teasing a new grand tourer (shown in full two months later as the McLaren GT), the company announced a McLaren Special Operations (MSO)-engineered version of the existing 720S Spider. Further to unveiling a 720S GT3 for a customer race team, Mc:Laren appeased core sports car fans by announcing that the company had no interest in following the trend to make an SUV. The spotlight shone on McLaren’s stand when the Senna GTR was displayed in its final form, having debuted as a concept one year prior, while McLaren exhibited the limited-production Speedtail for the first time after its earlier reveal., Joining this impressive display was the very McLaren 720S Spider offered here. Finished in Belize Blue with extensive application of exterior black carbon fibre trim, including MSO-defined carbon fibre options, the 720S was generously equipped by its maker to fully demonstrate the wealth of extras available to customers. Indeed, the Spider is finished with over £100,000-worth of optional add-ons, with the full specification list available to view on file., Built in left-hand drive and to German configuration, the 720S Spider was later taken to the United Kingdom, where it was registered for the road in February 2020. PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Rightly regarded as the most desirable variant of Ferrari’s seminal V-8, , the early fibreglass-bodied 308 GTBs offer a compelling blend of innovation, performance, rarity, and enduring style. Introduced in 1975 as the successor to the Dino 246, the 308 represented a turning point in Ferrari’s evolution, pairing Leonardo Fioravanti's striking Pininfarina design with a potent, transverse-mounted quad-cam V-8 engine to create one of the most engaging sports cars of its time., The earliest 308s were constructed using lightweight fibreglass bodywork—Vetroresina in Italian—before Ferrari transitioned to conventional steel construction in 1977. This innovative composite coachwork reduced weight dramatically, resulting in a curb weight of approximately 1,050 kilograms, nearly 150 kilograms lighter than its steel-bodied successors. The weight savings enhanced every aspect of the driving experience, from acceleration and agility to steering response and overall balance, qualities that continue to distinguish the earliest examples as the purest expressions of the 308. With production believed to total as few as 712 examples, these fibreglass-bodied cars rank among the rarest roadgoing Ferraris of the period., The configuration of this example, chassis number 20533, is rarer still. It is believed that only 154 ‘Vetroresina’ cars were delivered to the United Kingdom in right-hand drive. Since the transversely mounted, dry-sump, 2,926-cc engine breathed through the right-hand intake, the driver could lower their window to hear the induction bark in its purest form, directly over their shoulder, as they worked through the five-speed manual transmission with gated shifter., Finished in Rosso Chiaro over a Nero leather interior, the Ferrari is additionally equipped with power windows, a Radiomobile cassette stereo, and air conditioning. Supplied new to the United Kingdom, the 308 GTB’s first owner was one Mr Brand of Wallington, Surrey. The car passed to its second owner in July 1979 and they retained the Ferrari until January 2017, thus accounting for most of the vehicle’s life. The car is well documented by a collection of invoices detailing the service history in the UK between 1977 and 2023. The Ferrari is further accompanied by a selection of older MoT certicates, the newest of which documents an odometer reading of 12,263 miles in December 1984., This 308 GTB presents in wonderful condition today and is further accompanied by a tool kit, MoT certificates, and sale documents.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of 712 examples of the 308 GTB ‘Vetroresina’ made with fibreglass body panels; one of just 154 built in right-hand drive, Delivered new to the United Kingdom, Formerly in the care of a previous owner from 1979 to 2017, Powered by a 2.9-litre V-8 engine paired with a five-speed manual transmission, Classic colour combination of Rosso Chiaro over a Nero leather interior, Accompanied by invoices dated 1977 to 2023, MoT certificates, and sale documents

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Immediately preceding the switch to pop-up headlamps, just six right-hand-drive Ferrari 365 GTB/4 Daytona Berlinettas were reportedly built with the Plexiglass light cover while also featuring a leather-trimmed steering wheel and headrests. Among them, chassis number 14111 was completed on 10 February 1971 wearing Oro Chiaro paint over Beige Connolly hide., Delivered new to Australia via official marque dealership W H Lowe in Melbourne, this car was first owned by Mr Alan Watkins of Balwyn, Victoria before being acquired by Supreme Court Justice Stuart Murdoch. Sparingly driven under his long-term care, the Ferrari was serviced by veteran Lowe employee John W Allan of JW Allan Automotive, then sold in 2005 to another significant collector and placed into storage until 2012., Later appearing at several Australian concours events, chassis 14111 was imported into the United Kingdom via DK Engineering in 2014. The specialist additionally carried out Ferrari Classiche certification, with this car awarded its important “Red Book” in May 2015 that noted the presence of its matching-numbers body, gearbox, and V-12 engine., Displayed at Salon Privé and the Italian Car Day at Brooklands in 2014, the Daytona was submitted for sympathetic refurbishment. This included a 2017 change to period-correct Blue Sera Metallizzato and renewal of the brightwork by Ross Packard. Meanwhile, the interior was retrimmed by Horsham-based classic Ferrari expert O’Rourke Coachtrimmers in Burgundy Connolly hide with the seats featuring the correct ‘Daytona stripes’—the configuration in which the car presents today., Recent maintenance has been entrusted to Rardley Motors in Hampshire. A Quicksilver exhaust system was fitted and the vehicle underside cleaned in January 2025, between services conducted in June 2024 and January 2026. In September of this year, Riverside Performance Engineering replaced the starter motor and ice-blasted all four corners and the driveline., Testament to chassis 14111, the vendor previously owned the car, sold it, and bought it back, such was his admiration. Since then, the Ferrari is reported to have performed faultlessly on a recent road trip to Spain., Supporting this wonderful Daytona—alongside to its “Red Book”—the car is accompanied by a tool roll, owner’s guides, spart parts catalogue, Warranty Card, and original guarantee for the Voxon radio made out to the first owner, Mr Watkins. It also boasts air conditioning and still sits on the standard seven-inch wheels. The odometer reading of 29,758 miles at the time of cataloguing is believed to be genuine., Refurbished but never restored and an incredibly rare specification that is considered by some to be the sweet spot of the model. Chassis 14111 is truly among the most desirable of Daytonas in existence. It would make for an excellent candidate to enjoy as part of driving tours and further display events in time for Ferrari’s upcoming 80th anniversary celebrations.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: American apparel designer and vintage streetwear enthusiast Sean Wotherspoon took inspiration from Volkswagen’s short-lived Golf Mark 3 Harlequin Edition in creating the colour-block exterior of this one-off Land Rover Series II ‘Art Car’ developed in collaboration with a British customisation specialist., Wotherspoon rose to notoriety in the fashion and vintage streetwear space after his creative take on the Nike Air Max 97 won a Nike design contest and went on to become one of the most popular limited-edition trainers of the late-2010s. Its vivid colour palette and unusual materials are hallmarks of Wotherspoon’s personal style. Spurred by this success and a YouTube vlog series focused on his vintage streetwear store Round Two, Wotherspoon went on to collaborate with Adidas and other brands. In 2023, he partnered with Porsche to develop a Taycan art car, its interior lined in corduroy, cork, and recycled fishing nets, while the multi-colour exterior was finished in bold hues that Porsche added to its Exclusive Manufaktur paint-to-sample service., Wotherspoon first teamed up with a British customisation specialist in 2025 after meeting California-based venture capitalist Phillip Sarofim, a noted petrolhead whose collection includes the Aston Martin Bulldog and Lancia Stratos Zero by Bertone. Sarofim commissioned Wotherspoon to customise his rare 1973 Porsche 911 Carrera RS 2.7 with the help of a specialist. Like the Taycan, it featured a colour-block exterior and interior reupholstered in vintage denim, plaid, and corduroy, with the dashboard lined in cork material reportedly left over from the Porsche project., The one-of-a-kind Land Rover offered here was also executed in Wotherspoon’s signature kaleidoscopic style and plaid patchwork interior, once again overseen by the customisation specialist from March to July of 2025, completed with the help of a workshop in Essex. The left-hand-drive Series II was fitted with new 16-inch Wolf wheels wearing BF Goodrich All-Terrain T/A tyres and a modern stereo head unit with Apple CarPlay integration. Once finished, the car was shipped to California and displayed at Monterey Car Week in August 2025., The Land Rover has since benefitted from having the clutch refurbished and a new release bearing and master and slave cylinders installed by Tommy’s Motor Co of Essex in January 2026. Given its uniqueness and artful execution by a well-known streetwear designer, it would make for a notable collection piece.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Ferrari resisted rear-engined layouts in Formula 1 yet was at the forefront of the technology with its road cars, courtesy of the Dino 206 GT. Named in honour of Enzo Ferrari’s tragically dead son, Alfredino, the model was introduced in 1967. It was surpassed two years later by the 246 GT, the V-6 growing from 2 to 2.4-litres for a total output of 195 horsepower. In 1972, the targa-top GTS debuted. Only 1,274 were completed during a two-year lifecycle., Chassis number 07094 offered here is one of just 235 configured in right-hand drive for the United Kingdom. Ordered via Maranello Concessionaires, it was specified in Nero over a Rosso Connolly leather interior with Black carpets. Per confirmation of the original order and the research of marque historian Marcel Massini, available on file, the car featured Cromodora alloy wheels, air conditioning, and electric windows. According to Vehicle Production Data provided by Ferrari, the 246 GTS was supplied to the UK in September 1973., Official Ferrari dealer Lovett of Marlborough took delivery in November, prior to the car selling to first owner Andrew West. The Dino would appear at the Ferrari Owners' Club GB’s annual event at Brocket Hall in 1990 and was sold later that year by John Collins of Talacrest into long-term custodianship in Singapore. Part of a significant collection for 28 years, the Ferrari was the subject of thorough maintenance. Detailed spreadsheets notably log a repaint and interior refurbishment plus engine and suspension overhaul in 2022., Chassis 07094 was offered as part of a prominent Ferrari collection at RM Sotheby’s London sale in November 2023 and sold to the vendor. In their care, the Dino was reregistered in the UK in April 2024 and submitted to HR Owen in London and marque specialist Simon Furlonger for recommissioning. Invoices spanning June 2024 to February 2025 total almost £18,000 and document a refresh of the carburettors, brakes, and suspension. The wheels were also refurbished and the underside and suspension components detailed. Most recently, the Dino returned to Simon Furlonger in September 2026 for an annual service, wheel alignment, new fuel tank sender, plus tweaks to the door lock, bonnet release, and roof latch mechanisms. The accompanying invoice exceeds £2,160. Back in the UK, the Dino has passed its yearly MoT inspections, with the latest certificate issued in June 2026., Presented in its factory-correct Nero exterior finish over a black interior, the Dino 246 GTS retains its matching-numbers engine. It would make for a glamourous route into the open-top classic Ferrari driving experience.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: White socks, brown loafers, perfect heel-and-toe downshifts, and a speedometer needle that was off the dial around the Suzuka circuit. If you think of Ayrton Senna behind the wheel of anything other than a Grand Prix car, you think of him behind the wheel of the Honda NSX., The three-time Formula 1 Driver’s World Champion began cultivating his relationship with Honda in 1987. The Japanese marque replaced Renault in supplying the turbocharged 1.5-litre V-6 for Team Lotus, and Senna expertly deployed the circa 1,000 horsepower to end the year with two wins and 3rd place in the points. That paved the way for the Brazilian to sign for McLaren, now also powered by Honda, in 1988. He vanquished incumbent team-mate Alain Prost to clinch his first Driver’s title that season aboard the utterly dominant MP4-4., Meanwhile, away from the F1 paddock, Senna famously played a part in the evolution of Honda’s “New Sportscar Experimental”, as the firm sought to rival Ferrari and Porsche by creating a performance car that really could be driven and enjoyed every day. While testing the prototype, Senna judged the chassis to be "a little fragile". His precise feedback prompted Honda to stiffen the frame by 50 per cent and refine the suspension tuning., Come the start of 1991, Senna already counted two F1 Driver’s crowns and was about to embark on a campaign that would yield his third. Per an agreement between Honda Motor Company and the driver, Honda would provide an NSX to which Senna had access for personal use. Alongside a pair of black cars, there was chassis number T000233 offered here. Configured in Formula Red with a contrasting black roof over a black leather interior, it was imported by Honda Automobil de Portugal and registered on 22 March 1991 with the number “SX-25-59”. The NSX was stored in Lisbon and delivered to Senna every time he arrived in the country., Senna clearly made good use of the car during the European leg of the 1991 season—the F1 icon having bought a property in the Quinta do Lago resort. He commuted to the Portuguese Grand Prix at Estoril, a race for which he would qualify 3rd and finish 2nd, aboard chassis T000233 and it would feature in the 1992 documentary, , with Senna dumping the clutch and spinning up the rear wheels on camera. Perhaps most famously for “SX-25-59”, Senna was pictured in jeans and a buttoned-down shirt washing the car with a hosepipe., Ten months after Senna was killed at Imola, according to the accompanying certificate of records issued by the Lisbon Automobile Registry Office, the car was registered in the Portuguese capital city in February 1995 by Laboa Etablissement. A fax from Honda confirming this car’s Senna provenance, which has been reaffirmed by Honda Motor Europe, further notes that the NSX was under the care of its own dealership, Nipomotor, come September 1997. It was next bought by the owner of MSCAR Comércio de Automóveis SA, based in the Algarve city of Faro in November 2009, prior to being purchased by Mr Robert McFagan in 2013. He had the car freighted to the United Kingdom, where it was registered for use on the road in May 2016., The NSX made a poignant visit to Imola in 2019, marking 25th years since Senna’s fatal crash at the Italian venue, with Minardi F1 team founder and circuit boss Giancarlo Minardi in the driver’s seat. Captured on film and in iconic photographs, chassis T000233 is ready to be adored by a new motorsport enthusiast.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: To mark the 70th anniversary of famed Italian design house Pininfarina at the turn of the new millennium, the 550 Maranello coupé was in line for a convertible makeover. Gaining a rakish cutdown windscreen and losing the fixed roof, the resulting 550 Barchetta Pininfarina was officially first shown to the public by respective company bosses Luca di Montezemolo and Sergio Pininfarina during the 2000 Paris Motor Show., Due to the number four being considered unlucky in parts of East Asia, the story goes that Ferrari decided to fractionally increase its originally forecasted production allocation from 444 to 448 examples. The upshot was that another handful of customers were fortunate enough to experience the open-air thrills of a naturally aspirated 5.5-litre V-12 engine delivering its 479 brake horsepower via a six-speed, open-gate, manual transmission., The car offered here is numbered “138” from the run of only 448 examples of the 550 Barchetta Pininfarina. Adding to its rarity, this is one of reportedly just 48 that were configured from the factory in right-hand-drive form. Attractively finished in Rosso Corsa over an interior sporting Nero Connolly leather and matching-colour carpets, it was further specified with red brake callipers sitting behind the five-spoke split-rim wheels., Fitted with instruments reading in kilometres, the 550 Barchetta Pininfarina was delivered new to Hong Kong in June 2001 via the Italian Motors Ltd importer. Per the accompanying Warranty Card, the Ferrari was handed over to its first owner, Mr Poon Kin Lap, on 3 July., According to Ferrari service records, the 550 Barchetta Pininfarina was submitted to Naza Italia in Malaysia for maintenance. From a July 2012 appointment, the car was noted to have only covered 54 kilometres. Five months later, in November, it was awarded prestigious Ferrari Classiche certification. The supporting “Red Book” recorded the presence of its matching-numbers body, engine, and gearbox., Additional services were carried out by Naza Italia in January 2015 (the Ferrari logged with 65 kilometres), May 2019 (111 kilometres), March 2020 (111 kilometres), and November 2021 (545 kilometres). The following year, the 550 Barchetta Pininfarina was brought to the United Kingdom. To round out 2022, it was sent to Ferrari dealer H R Owen in South London in December for a major service. The corresponding invoice—available on file—details an engine and gearbox oil and filter change, renewal of the brake fluid, plus the important installation of a new cambelt, auxiliary belt, and tensioners. A fresh battery was fitted, the geometry checked, and the boot struts replaced as part of work totalling £8,692., At the time of its visit to the H R Owen, the 550 Barchetta Pininfarina was recorded with 562 kilometres displayed. Having been stored thereafter, the Ferrari heads to RM Sotheby’s London auction with 571 kilometres on the odometer at the time of cataloguing. Further to its Warranty Card and “Red Book”, the car is supplied with its owner’s guides in their leather folio, Certificate of Origin, canvas roof, indoor car cover, tool and tyre inflator kits, plus the two Barchetta helmets with their accompanying dust cover bags and carry cases., Courtesy of an incredibly limited production run, the opportunity to acquire any 550 Barchetta Pininfarina marks a special occasion for the Cavallino collector. However, this barely driven right-hand-drive example—offered in its factory-correct Rosso Corsa over Nero colour combination, further to touting Ferrari Classiche certification and its generous bevy of accessories—is surely difficult to surpass. Bidders should not overlook their chance to buy such a well-preserved example that presents just as it left the Maranello factory gates some 25 years ago.
