PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: As one of Ferrari’s most celebrated grand touring models, the 275 GTB combined formidable performance with Pininfarina styling and Scaglietti craftsmanship, redefining the concept of the sporting, . Among these already coveted cars, those specified with lightweight aluminium coachwork occupy a particularly desirable position, combining rarity with a direct connection to Ferrari’s competition-focused engineering philosophy., According to the research of model expert and respected collector Dyke Ridgley, chassis number 08059 is one of approximately 80 long-nose, two-cam examples fitted from new with alloy coachwork. According to a report on file by noted marque historian Marcel Massini, this car was completed in December 1965, equipped with triple carburettors and instruments calibrated in kilometres. Its aluminium coachwork was finished in Giallo Fly, complemented by an interior upholstered in Bleu Vaumol leather., The Ferrari was sold new to Stabilimenti Chimico Farmaceutico G Alberani, a pharmaceutical company in Bologna. The company retained the 275 for approximately 18 months, during which time the car was submitted to Ferrari’s Assistenza Clienti in Modena for service., In May 1967, G Alberani sold the Ferrari to its second owner, Simona Messori of Reggio Emilia. The GTB subsequently returned to Ferrari’s Assistenza Clienti on five further occasions through August 1968. Its Italian registration was cancelled in January 1969 in preparation for export., By 1973, the Ferrari had been acquired by marque collector Lee Wilson of Fort Wayne, Indiana. During his ownership, chassis number 08059 was displayed at local and national Ferrari Club of America gatherings, often alongside his 250 GT California Spider Competizione. In 1982, Mr Wilson presented the Alloy at a gathering at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, and two years later the car was exhibited at the Auburn-Cord-Duesenberg Museum in Auburn, Indiana., In 1986, the Ferrari was sold to Shin Takei, a respected collector of sporting automobiles then based in Sherman Oaks, California. According to Ferrari Owners Club USA membership records, Mr Takei remained the caretaker of the 275 GTB until at least 1993., In 2003, the car was acquired by Philippe Lancksweert, the noted Belgian collector and former partner in Jacques Swaters’ Garage Francorchamps, Ferrari’s celebrated Belgian distributorship. Mr Lancksweert commissioned a comprehensive restoration and preparation for historic competition. The highly respected Bacchelli & Villa attended to the chassis and aluminium coachwork, which was refinished in Giallo, while Tappezzeria Luppi retrimmed the interior in blue leather., Historic competition preparation was entrusted to Dutch specialist Roelofs Engineering. This included the installation of six Weber carburettors, an external fuel filler, interior safety roll cage, and 15-inch wheels, readying chassis 08059 for participation in some of Europe’s most demanding historic events., In conjunction with this work, the owner applied for Ferrari factory certification. In April 2004, chassis 08059 was issued its Ferrari Classiche "Red Book", documenting the presence of its matching-numbers chassis, engine, and coachwork. Mr Lancksweert also applied for FIA papers in May 2003, preparing the car for an active career in historic competition. In April 2004, the Ferrari began its modern motorsport career with participation in the Tour Auto., A month later, the car was acquired by the consigning owner, a longtime Ferrari enthusiast and collector, who has now retained the car for 22 years. During this unusually long period of continuous ownership, the 275 has been extensively enjoyed in major European events, including the 2004 Le Mans Classic and numerous editions of the Tour Auto through to 2024. The GTB also participated in the 2017 Modena Cento Ore Classic and, while in Italy, was displayed at the Motor Gallery in Modena., Throughout this long-term ownership chassis 08059 has remained an actively enjoyed example of the alloy-bodied 275 GTB, rather than simply a static collection piece. Thus demonstrating the performance and versatility for which Ferrari’s great 1960s, are renowned., Today, this car combines several of the attributes most prized in a 275 GTB: rare factory aluminium coachwork, desirable long-nose configuration, Ferrari Classiche certification, matching-numbers major components as documented by its "Red Book", respected restoration work, substantial historic-event participation, and more than two decades of continuous ownership., The Ferrari is accompanied by its Ferrari Classiche documentation and "Red Book", FIA historic competition documentation from two ownership periods, and a detailed history report by Marcel Massini., Ideally suited to continued participation in leading historic events, yet equally compelling for Ferrari gatherings and concours presentation, chassis 08059 represents an exceptional opportunity to acquire a well-documented, factory-alloy example of one of Ferrari’s defining 1960s, , one whose long-term ownership and extensive event history have allowed it to be enjoyed precisely as its sporting character intended.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of approximately 80 long-nose, two-cam 275 GTBs factory-fitted with lightweight aluminium coachwork, Completed in December 1965 in the striking factory colour combination of Giallo Fly over Bleu Vaumol leather, Comprehensively restored in 2003 by respected Italian specialists Bacchelli & Villa and Tappezzeria Luppi, Prepared for historic competition by Roelofs Engineering, including the fitment of a six-Weber-carburettor induction system, Ferrari Classiche certified in 2004; matching-numbers chassis, engine, and coachwork documented by accompanying "Red Book", Offered after 22 years of continuous ownership by the vendor, Extensively enjoyed in leading European historic events, including the Le Mans Classic, Tour Auto, and Modena Cento Ore, Supplied with FIA historic competition documentation, and a history report by Marcel Massini

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Finished by the factory in the iconic 997.2-generation GT3 RS colour scheme of Grey Black with Guards Red accents, this car was delivered new via Porsche Centre Leicester in January of 2011 to a member of the Bamford family, one of Britain's most well-known motoring families. The car was outfitted in Clubsport specification with a roll cage and bucket seats in addition to options including red instrument dials, black-faced stopwatch, Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes, Sound Package Plus, top-tinted windscreen, six-point harness, lighter halogen headlights, Sport Chrono Plus package, and large helpings of interior trim comprising Alcantara and carbon fibre., The GT3 RS remained with its original owner for eight years, finally selling in 2018 having accrued approximately 1,000 miles in their ownership. Remaining in the UK ever since with a handful of careful owners, the Porsche shows just 1,992 miles at the time of cataloguing, meaning it is surely among the lowest-mileage examples in the country., The car’s last annual service was carried out by Porsche Centre York in May 2026, at which point the odometer read 1,970 miles. PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: Following the critical acclaim of the 360 Challenge Stradale in the early 2000s, Ferrari sought to replicate the success by producing a harder-edged and faster version of its latest supercar, the F430. None other than seven-time Formula 1 World Champion Michael Schumacher was enlisted to assist the engineers in Maranello with development. Just two years after the launch of F430, the man himself unveiled the 430 Scuderia at the 2007 Frankfurt Auto Show., The upgrades were numerous throughout. The naturally aspirated 4.3-litre V-8 received higher-compression pistons, new exhaust manifolds, and revisions to the cooling. That increased output to 510 brake horsepower, 25 more than standard. Hardware and software revisions for the F1-SuperFast 2 paddle-shift transmission meant that gearchanges were over in just 60 milliseconds, enabling the 430 Scuderia to reach 60 mph from a standstill in just 3.3 seconds before topping out at 198 mph., Reducing weight was also key to the philosophy of the 430 Scuderia. The normal leather-laden interior was stripped down, a Lexan engine cover replaced the glass item, and bespoke lightweight alloy wheels were fitted. This helped the car shed a staggering 100 kilograms. In addition, having been lowered by 15 millimetres, further to sporting a new rear diffuser and larger rear spoiler, the 430 Scuderia reportedly lapped faster around Fiorano than the flagship Enzo., Completed in May 2008, this 430 Scuderia is one of just 165 examples built in right-hand drive for the United Kingdom. It was specified in Rosso Corsa, with the optional racing stripe, over a Nero Alcantara interior featuring carbon fibre seats. The lightweight wheels were factory-finished in gold and complemented by Giallo Modena brake callipers., Per the accompanying Warranty Card, the 430 Scuderia was supplied to its first owner via official Ferrari dealership Stratstone Manchester on 17 July 2008. Through to March 2024, the car has been maintained by a host of respected specialists, including Graypaul Nottingham, Meridien Modena, and Dick Lovett Swindon, prior to returning to Stratstone Manchester. Most recently, in June 2025, the 430 Scuderia was serviced by Simon Furlonger. Further offered with its owner’s guides and manuals in their folio, tool and tyre inflator kits, plus indoor cover, the car displayed a mere 5,938 miles at the time of cataloguing., As a prized Ferrari special-edition built in right-hand-drive form, this 430 Scuderia offers bidders the opportunity to acquire an ever-increasingly collectable Prancing Horse.

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: A hat-trick of consecutive victories in the 24 Hours of Le Mans between 1955 and 1957 ensures that the Jaguar D-Type ranks among the most revered competition cars of all time. The marque later withdrew from the World Sportscar Championship owing to a rule change that limited engine capacity to three litres. As a result, to recoup some of its investment and to target the North American market’s wealthy amateur racers, 25 of its D-Type chassis were slated to be converted for road use., By adding a windscreen, mohair roof, luggage rack, passenger door, side screens, and chromed bumpers—while removing the rear tail fin and cockpit divider—the legendary XKSS was born. Just 16 would leave the Browns Lane factory before a fire broke out, destroying the nine remaining chassis., An expertly executed copy of those original cars, this XKSS Recreation started life in 1967 as an E-Type Series 1 4.2-Litre Roadster that was sold in New York. Subsequently acquired by the consigning owner and registered in the United Kingdom from April 2015, chassis number 1E16062 was swiftly submitted to Jaguar race car specialist Jim Tester of Team Racing & Engineering in Daventry for transformation., As part of the process carried out through to 2017, the riveted aluminium sheet bodywork was crafted by Robert Gregson while a 3.4-litre dry-sump XK straight-six engine—period-correct type for the XKSS, as also found in the Mark 2, S-Type, XK 120, and more—was fitted with triple Weber 45 DCOE carburettors and paired with an all-synchro gearbox. Finished in black, sporting 16-inch Dunlop peg-drive wheels, over a red leather interior with race-style harnesses, competition seats, and a padded transmission tunnel, the XKSS Recreation would immediately enter dry storage. Pulled out from its resting place in 2024, the car was recommissioned and road tested by Martin Greaves of Classic Performance Engineering, the renowned classic race car workshop based in Silverstone., Painstakingly reimagined, this XKSS Recreation presents an excellent opportunity to acquire a recently recommissioned and excellently presented homage to one of the world’s rarest and most sought-after vehicles.

LOT_SUMMARY: Expert recreation of the famed Jaguar XKSS, the road-going relation of the D-Type, Constructed between 2015 and 2017 by noted Jaguar race car specialist Jim Tester, Built upon an E-Type Series 1 donor chassis; powered by a 3.4-litre XK straight-six, a period-correct engine type for the XKSS, Dry-stored since completion until 2024; recommissioned by Classic Performance Engineering of Silverstone, Hand-formed aluminium bodywork finished in black over a red leather interior

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: It took almost two decades for Porsche to properly reveal the missing link between Formula 1 and what is arguably the greatest road car in its illustrious history. At the 2018 Goodwood Festival of Speed, the unraced LMP 2000 prototype made its long overdue public debut., The open-top racer was conceived to take on Audi in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. At the heart of the project was a naturally aspirated V-10, which had been secretly developed in the early 1990s with the intention of powering the Footwork F1 team. While that topflight career never came to pass for the engine, the concept was refined from 3.5- to 5.5-litre capacity during the gestation of the LMP 2000. Yet again, the programme would be abandoned before competing in anger. The official reason given was to direct funds to the nascent Cayenne SUV., Fortunately, however, the competition-bred V-10 would finally earn its time in the spotlight, sitting midships in the Porsche Carrera GT. Entering a limited production of 1,270 units in 2003, the flagship hypercar produced 603 horsepower. Not only was that figure accompanied by one of the most celebrated howling soundtracks, but it was delivered through a six-speed manual transmission—the wood-topped gear lever a tribute to the all-conquering 917., Although the powertrain is the star of the show, the Carrera GT also incorporated cutting-edge material science. A carbon fibre monocoque and subframe were accompanied by carbon-ceramic brakes and a three-disc carbon fibre racing clutch. The ultra-lightweight forged magnesium wheels were fixed in place by centre-locking bolts that were colour-coded for each side of the car., Fast forward another 20 years and the mothballed LMP 2000 has been uncovered and restored by Porsche to running condition, while the Carrera GT has only doubled down on its hallowed status as a performance car icon. More powerful than a Ford GT, purer than a Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren, and arguably more driver-focused than a Ferrari Enzo, it is considered by many to be the standout model even among its glittering contemporaries., Configured for country code “C00”, the Carrera GT offered here was built in left-hand drive for its home market. Holding a 17 February 2004 date of production, the car was finished in GT Silver Metallic over Dark Grey leather. It was specified with desirable XT driver and passenger bucket seats, air conditioning, and a Porsche Online Pro CD radio system., The Carrera GT was delivered to its first owner on 8 April via Porsche Centre Munich, although its time in Germany was brief. Per the accompanying service book, which shows 13 stamps, this car was exported to Japan by September. That month, it was submitted to Porsche Centre Aoyama Setagaya with 1,267 kilometres recorded. It returned to the same franchise on seven other occasions, before the Muraoka Motor Company Ltd in Warabi City assumed responsibility for maintenance. The last visit to the Saitama Prefecture workshop came in 2017, with the car then noted at 38,400 kilometres., Since October 2021, the Carrera GT has been registered for road use in the United Kingdom. It was initially retained by the previous owner, based in Guildford. In December of that year, they sent the car to Porsche Group Operations Centre Reading for an engine-out major service, which included the renewal of the brake fluid and installation of a new thermostat housing. The corresponding invoice, which is available to view on file, totals £13,723., Acquired by the vendor in June 2022, the Carrera GT returned to Porsche Centre Reading in April 2025. For this appointment, two new near-side front rod ball joint boots were fitted and the tyre pressure-monitoring sensors replaced. In addition, at this time, the APA3 recall procedure was performed free of charge alongside a minor service and the fitment of four new tyres for a final cost of £3,621., The car secured a first-time pass with no advisories upon its latest MoT inspection in June 2026. At the time of cataloguing, the Carrera GT displayed 25,694 miles on the odometer and is set for a 111-point inspection by Porsche Centre Reading in October., Beautifully specified in GT Silver Metallic over a Dark Grey leather interior and diligently maintained throughout its travels, this UK-registered Carrera GT presents in unmodified, excellent condition. Whether it is to be driven on the limit or enjoyed as part of a significant collection, the car awaits its next doting custodian.

LOT_SUMMARY: One of only 1,270 examples of the revered, V-10, manual transmission hypercar, Delivered new to Germany, followed by ownership in Japan and the United Kingdom, Specified with GT Silver Metallic paintwork over a Dark Grey leather interior, Factory-fitted XT bucket seats, air conditioning, and Porsche Online Pro CD radio, Most recent service performed by Porsche Centre Reading in April 2025, The odometer displayed 25,694 miles from new at the time of cataloguing

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: A key instalment in Ferrari’s statement “Big Six” lineup—beginning with the 288 GTO and rounded out by the F50, Enzo, hybrid LaFerrari, and latest F80—the F40 stands as one of the most significant Prancing Horses ever made. By extension, it counts as one of the most important and special automotive creations of all time., Famously, the F40 was the final design to be signed off by company founder Enzo Ferrari. Publicly introduced at the Frankfurt Motor Show in 1987, it was initially forecast for a production run of 400 examples in celebration of the marque’s 40th anniversary. However, that figure eventually stretched to 1,315 units as customer interest skyrocketed., Little wonder, given a lightweight Kevlar and carbon fibre construction being propelled by a twin-turbocharged 2.9-litre V-8 that delivered circa 478 horsepower to achieve 201 mph. That top speed rating placed the F40 as the fastest road car in the world upon its launch., The inspiration behind the project was entry into the FIA’s Group B competition regulations. While the category in the World Rally Championship was ultimately cancelled before the F40 could turn a wheel in anger, its innate motorsport pedigree lived on in the form of the F40 LM. The model would compete in the IMSA SportsCar Championship in the United States before trading paint with McLaren F1 GTRs in the celebrated BPR Global GT Series., The early production F40 offered here, chassis number 78623, was completed to European specification. According to the records of Ferrari historian Marcel Massini, the Maranello factory commenced the build on 14 September 1988. Wearing the universal F40 colour scheme of Rosso Corsa over seats trimmed in Stoffa Vigogna red wool fabric, it was finished on 13 December and supplied new in its home country, with the delivery fulfilled by the famed Sa Mo Car dealership in Rome, Italy., Listed on a vehicle history report, which is available to view on file, chassis 78623 would soon relocate to Japan. As part of its long-term residency in the country, the F40 was registered via the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism in April 1994. Later in its life, most likely while in Japan, the Ferrari was modified to resemble the competition-specification F40 LM—as the car presents today., This F40 is further documented by an inspection report, which bidders are encouraged to review, that was compiled in July 2026 by respected marque expert GTO Engineering and an RM Sotheby’s Specialist. The report lists that the front and rear clamshells are replacements, styled in the fashion of the F40 LM but not sourced from the race car’s original builder Michelotto. The doors and sections of the floor are non-original, but the lightweight Lexan sliding windows, Kevlar bulkhead, and roof all notably appear to be factory items., While the car was cosmetically changed in line with the design of the F40 LM, the front and rear suspension on chassis 78623 retain the road car’s standard setup with rubber bushings. An air jack system has been integrated alongside non-standard disc brakes, radiator fans, and water-oil cooler. The engine heat shielding, fuel delivery system, intercooler, and wastegate setup are not original. An original, standard radiator and five-spoke OZ LM wheels are fitted., For the interior, this F40 is equipped with an LM-style digital dashboard and runs a MoTeC electronic control unit—the original Marelli boxes remain in situ. The standard seats have been replaced with red-trimmed OMP items fitted with Momo race-style harnesses. The lever for the five-speed, open-gate manual transmission is topped with a carbon fibre gear knob from an F50. The car also features an F50 rearview mirror., Upon inspection, the F40 started instantly and ran without fault but was not road tested. Due to the technical and visual complexity of this car, please speak to an RM Sotheby’s Specialist for further information,, Chassis 78623 is observed to retain its matching-numbers engine and manual transmission with standard synchromesh. Meanwhile, the digital odometer displayed 30,398 kilometres at the time of cataloguing. Please note: the original odometer is not present, nor any records to warrant this figure. The car is supplied with a spare set of wheels and tyres. Offered directly from the current Japanese custodian, it has been shipped to the United Kingdom for the auction. Relevant import taxes will need to be paid should the car remain in the UK., A coveted early production F40 that was built for the European market and significantly boasting its matching-numbers engine and transmission, chassis 78623 stands out as a prime candidate for a restoration back to its original road specification. Alternatively, the car could stay as is or serve as an ideal basis for a variety of upgrade opportunities.

LOT_SUMMARY: Desirable early production F40 fitted with lightweight Lexan sliding windows, European-market example delivered new to Rome via Sa Mo Car in December 1988, Retains its matching-numbers twin-turbocharged V-8 engine and five-speed transaxle, Modified to resemble an F40 LM prior to current ownership, Supplied with July 2026 report by GTO Engineering plus spare wheel/tyre set, A prime candidate to be fully restored back to factory road specification

PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION: In 1993, Ferrari introduced a competition-prepared variant of its 348 supercar for use in a new single-make race series dubbed the Ferrari Challenge. The series evolved over the years, offering a home for track-only versions of roadgoing V-8 models, continuing to iterations of the F355 in 1995 and 360 Modena in 2000. Since these cars were exclusively for the circuit, the factory received sizeable demand for a commensurate entry that could be legally driven on public roads., Accordingly, the 360 Challenge Stradale of 2003 was envisioned as a street-legal version of the Challenge racer—although in actuality was a modified 360 Modena designed for part-time track use. It shaved a considerable amount of weight from the base model with the removal of sound insulation and other creature comforts., The new Challenge Stradale was equipped with advanced mechanical elements such as a Formula 1-style paddle-shift transaxle, uprated carbon-composite brakes, lower and stiffer suspension, heftier anti-roll bar, and a modified V-8 engine. The retuned mill now developed higher compression to yield a dividend of 25 additional horses, for a total output of 425 horsepower., Ferrari ultimately built fewer than 1,300 examples of the prodigious 360 Challenge Stradale. It became an instant classic among Maranello racing connoisseurs, as the purest and fastest example of the already-dazzling 360 Modena., Claiming a life of regular service attention and modest driving use, chassis number 135973 offered here was completed in January 2004. It was finished in Nero Daytona paint, featuring the Italian-themed Challenge Stradale stripes, and appointed with Scuderia shields and black-painted brake callipers. According to an, on file, the Ferrari was delivered new in January 2004 to an enthusiast based in Alessandria, Italy. In November 2008, the car passed to a specialist dealer and was then exported outside of its home country in 2012., In 2014, the Ferrari was purchased by a collector in the United Kingdom, who imported the car to England and registered it in December 2014. Service invoices from this period demonstrate attention by marque dealer Stratstone Ferrari Manchester, including replacement of the timing belt., The following January, the Challenge Stradale was acquired by the consigning owner. Under their care, it has been dutifully maintained with regular services by marque dealer H R Owen, as well as additional work by specialist Bob Houghton (as clarified by invoices on file and stamps in the car’s warranty booklet). This included the replacement of the timing belt and auxiliary belts in October 2024 and an annual service with software update of the ECUs in January 2026., During the vendor’s 11-year ownership, they claim that the Ferrari has never been used on a track. MoT test certificates clarify the car has accrued only 3,403 kilometres since October 2014. Similarly, they understand that the prior owner never drove the car on circuit either. Upon purchasing the Challenge Stradale, the clutch wear was noted at 3 per cent (observed December 2014). It may be logically concluded, therefore, that the car has largely avoided hard driving, which is surely a major factor in its current pristine state of condition., Accompanied by its owner’s manuals in the proper pouch, this beautifully presented 360 Challenge Stradale displayed just 14,925 kilometres on the odometer at the time of cataloguing. Ideal for enjoyment on circuits or presentation at supercar gatherings and Ferrari events, this exceptional, well-maintained, track-ready, would make for a fantastic acquisition for any enthusiastic, .
